cells.date: Śaka 1258( ashṭa-pañcha-yugaļa-ēka )Dhātri, Mādhava śu. 7=1336 A.D., April 18, Thursday
cells.remarks: Copy of a copper-plate record. Records a royal grant of the village Yāraguđi in Tummadāmala-sthala of Koṇdakāmala-Vallūru-sīme, in the Yakuri-nivṛitti (?) belonging to Ghanaśailapuri-rājya, to Pampā Virūpāksha, of Bhāradvāja-gōtra,Āślāyana-śutra and Bahvṛicha-śākhā, son of Bhāskara,the chief (?) of Arēkere, during the phālābhishēka festival of Pampā Virūpāksha Mahēśvara. Also records the grant of Chiravārapalli for the service of god Mahēśvara of Śrīśaila. The inscription was engraved by śāsanāchārya Nāgadēva. It gives a genealogical account of the king as follows : Bukka m Māgāmbikā→Saṅgama m Mānāmbikā →Harihara, Kampa, Bukka, Māra and Mudda. It says that Harihara received the grace of god Virūpāksha and also met sage Vidyāraṇya at whose instance he built a new town ( Puri ) named Vidyā.

cells.object: On a stone in the place called  nađamagadđe .
cells.remarks: Records the gift of dasavanda , free of all imposts, 130 Śiṅgava-gadvāṇa and some land below the sluice, a horse and bracelets to Peda Bayiravōja and Pina Bayiravōja for having dug a channel from Peda Nandisariyūru to Tirumañi village belonging to Kārakuṛiki-sthaļa in Penugoṇđa-rājya. The gift was made on the condition that these should be returned if water did not flow in the channel from Annadāna-muchađi to Immađiyūru. The channel was dug by the direction of Jommādēvi, daughter of Virūpādēvi and grand-daughter of Bukka-mahārāya and by the order of Nāgaraja, son of Bommarāja, her minister as also Māyi-nāyaka.

cells.date: Šaka...., Sādhāraṇa, Jyēshṭha ba. 13=1430 A.D, June 18, Sunday, the Šaka year being 1352
cells.object: On a stone near the village entrance.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of land (specified) probably by Lakkaṇṇa-vođeya, as a mānya , to Chiyiya Bassi-seṭṭi, the paṭṭaṇasvāmi of the fair ( sante ) which was established by the sālumūle of the 56 countries with all the cultivators and pañchāļas . The artisans like the ironsmiths, carpenters, goldsmiths, washermen and barbers were exempted from payment of taxes as also sale and purchase of cattle, horse, slaves ( totlu ). The village Maragallu which belonged to the Jumjiru-gaṇas was situated in Tēkal-nāđu of Muļabāgilu.

cells.date: Śaka 1609, Jaya, śu. 5, Śaura Karkaṭaka. These details do not tally. Śaka 1609=1687-88 A.D., is too late for any of the Vijayanagara rulers. The cyclic year Jaya occurs only in the reign-period of Veñkaṭapati 1, the Śaka year being 1516. Even then Śaura Karkaṭaka fell on July 1, Monday, 1594 A.D., when the  tithi  was śu. 1 in the month of Śrāvaṇa.
cells.object: On a stone in the peepul tree platform in front of the Raṅgasvāmi temple.
cells.remarks: Aṇakanūru Records the grant of land at Aṇakanūru, by the king for the daily feeding at the Rāmz-nuja-kūṭa in the temple of Raṅganātha. The donees were Parāśara-bhaṭṭa of Harita-gōtra and Āpastambha-sūtra who received half of the gifted land and Tirupati-bhaṭṭa, Aṭagha-śiṅgari-bhaṭṭa, kumāra Veñkaṭa-bhaṭa and Varadāchārya.

cells.date: Šaka 1293, Virōdhikřit, Kārttika šu. 15, Friday, lunar eclipse=1371 A.D., October 24
cells.object: On a stone near Rājappa's tank.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of riceland as kaťtu-gođagi , for having built the Periya-samudra in the name of Periyava-nāyakiti, mother of Hiriya Chile-nāyaka and Chika Chile-nāyaka, sons of Pōcha-nāyaka of Pogarūru. Also records the grant of lands to four individuals each getting one cart ( bhaṇđi ) and states that the first three yields were exempted from taxes whereafter the palace was to be paid part of the yield ( vāra ) at the rate of three koļagas per kamđuga . Pōcheya-nāyaka bears several titles like Kāvēri vallabha , Pekkađru-rājula okkettu gamđa and Chōļa-kaťaka-cch.i yekāra . Nāgaņņa-vođeya described as Kantikārarāyaragamđa was governing Sādali-rājya. Chile-nāyaka who received one bhaṇđi of land gifted the same among several Brāhmaņas (named) as vrittis . Birōja, son of Dēvōja wrote the record.

cells.date: Śaka...., Krōdhana, Mārgaśira śu. 1, Va=1385 A.D., November 4, Saturday, the Śaka year being 1307.
cells.object: On a stone in the Masalti Muniyappa's field.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of the village Muṭṭūru for offerings and services of god Varadarāja of Kaṁjāvara, by Dēpaṇṇa-vođeya, son of Nāgaṇṇa-vođeya. The latter is described as Khaṇtikārarāyara-gaṁḍa . Cf. KN 1274 above Above this record is engraved another epigraph which states that it is the charity ( dharma ) of Rācharasa. This may not be connected with the record noted here.

cells.date: Śaka 1511, expressed by the chronogram  bhū-śāśāmka śara-kshōṇi , Sarvadhāri, Māgha śu. 12 = 1589 A.D., January 18, Saturday.
cells.object: On a set of 5 copper-plates in the possession of Tirumalāchārya, the priest of the same temple.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of Mēlagrāma in Ba||agere-sthaļa of Penugoṇḍa-mahārājya, by the king to Apparasa-mahāmantri, son of Kōnapēndra and grandson of Apparasa belonging to Gautama-gōtra and Āpastambha-sūtra. The record was composed by Krishna-kavi, son of Gaṇapaya and grandson of Sabhāpati, and engraved by Virāchārya. The record gives a genecalogical account of the king.

cells.object: On a stone to the right of the main entrance to the Bhimēśvara temple.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of money due from the villages belonging to god Bhimēśvara towards Kāṇike , kaṇdāya etc. for offerings and other services of that god. The grant was made by Śakārśa's (?) son (name lost) to Rāmā-bhaṭṭa, sen of Chivanā-bhaṭṭa when Bhāskara-dēva, o n of Dammathāsēni (?) Jāmarasa was the manager ( pāruptya ) of the temple. The deity Bhimēśvara is said to have been consecrated by Bhimasēna at Ekachakrapura alias Kayivāra. The record is said to have been set up during the adhikāra-pārupatya (manager of office ?) of Viramarasa.

cells.object: On a natural boulder below the dilapidated Narasimhasvāmi temple.
cells.remarks: Damaged. cells.date: Śaka 1266, expressed by the chronogram  rasa-bhū-nayana-indu , Tāraṇa, Chaitra śu.9=1344 A.D., March 23, Tuesday.
cells.object: On a set of 3 copper-plates in the possession of Jaṭāvallabha, the  patel  of Ramāpura.
cells.remarks: Registers a royal grant of the (village) Peñchukalladinna alias Bukkarāyapura, on the bank of the Pinākini, in Kōđuru Penna-māgaṇi, of Guttidurga-rājya to the poet Nāchana Sōma, belonging to Bhāradvāja-anvaya, Āpastambha-sūtra and Yajuś-śākha, described as ashṭa-bhāshā-kavi well-versed in all the Ágamas and the 18 Purāṇas . This poet further divided the village into 110 vrittis and retaining 36 vrittis for himself as yajamāna-bhāga , distributed the remaining among other Brāhmaṇas named. Mallaṇārā-dhya, son of Kōṭidēvārādhyāchārya of Ātrēya-gōtra and Yajuś-śākhā composed the record which was engraved by Nāgidēva. The record says that the king was ruling Vidyānagara (founded by) Vidyāraṇya.

cells.date: Śaka 1212, Bhāva, Chaitra śu. 5, Budhavāra=1334 A.D., March 9, Wednesday, f.d.t. .90
cells.object: On brass plates in the possession of Chikka Saṇṇakempa.
cells.remarks: Saňkaragonđa, Timmanagöđa and others, the seven sons of Vulela-rāya, king of Māṇaka-paṭṇa, visited Vira-pratāpa Bukka-bhūpatirāya, Dēvarāya and Guṇđamarāya and presented 12,000 adherents, 100 horsemen, 50 foot soldiers, 4 howdah-bearing elephants, 7 herds of cows, 7 carts and one cart full of money. The king conferred on them horse, umbrella, chāmora , hīmu-peṇđe and 3 howdah-elephants. After their return these gauđas made a grant of horse and 20 varahas to the officiating priest of the Kuruđi village. And in the treasury of their palace they placed 7 vessels full of money on the south-east with golden images and bronze sacrificial vessels. They also made grants of lands. The money they spent on the village was 10030 Rāmaṭeṭmki varohas , 2000 Lakshmipati varahas and puttalikas . The inscription was engraved by Virāchāri of Būdagal-nāđu by the order of Bukkarāya Guṇđamārāyal and Ambhĵjarāya and made it over to Timmaṇa-göđu. Obviously spurious.

cells.remarks: Chōlēnahaļļi A set of two copper-plates in the possession of the shanbhog of the village. Kolar Distriet It contains the genealogy of the king who is said to be the son of Vijayabhūpati and Nārāyaṇāmbikā. cells.remarks: Records the grant of 21 gadyāṇas for offerings to god Bhairava of Sihatti for a new car festival to be held for 9 days and for the expenses of extra sacrifices etc., to Gūliya and other priests. The gift money was being received by the donor as kāvalu, kali, bēdige, tribute etc. from the donees to the Kōlāla-sime, belonging to the chieftaincy of the donor, mahāmaṇdalēśvara Narasayyadēva-mahā-arasa, son of Timmayadēva-mahā-arasu (Chikka Timmarāja). The gift was made for the merit of the king and the donor's parents.

cells.date: Šaka 1328, Vyaya, Mārgaśira šu. 15, Thursday, lunar eclipse = 1406 A.D., November 25.
cells.object: On the south wall of the Kaṇvēšvara temple.
cells.remarks: Belļūru Records a grant of the villages Bayichanakuṇte and Tujilahaļli alias Vishṇuvardhana-chaturvēd'maṅgala, by Malidēva-rāne, son of Niđava-rāne by the order of Dēvarāya-ođeya, son of mahāpradhāna Bommaṇa-daṇnayaka. The grant was inclusive of income from taxes on houses, mađavaļike, kāṇike etc. Also records a gift of the tank Bidirakuṇte and the lands below it in Biļimāranahaļi and the tank Māraguđikuṇte and the lands below it in Bairagoṇđanahaļi belonging to Šrigirinātha by Đāvula Sūre-nāyaka for the same god. The two tanks and lands were converted into one village called Dēvarāyapura.

cells.date: Šaka 1499, Isvara, Phālguṇa ba. 30, Saturday, solar eclipse =1578 A.D., March 8
cells.object: On a set of two copper-plates in the possession of the  šānabhōga .
cells.remarks: Records the grant of three villages Voratūru, Soruhuṇise and Hāruvahalli in Voratūru-hōbaļi of Beṅgaļūru-sime by Hiriya Kempe-gauđa, son of Kempanañje-gauđa and grandson of Nañje-gauđa, the chief ( prabhu ) of Yalahakka-nāđu. The donee Tirumalayya, son of Timmappayya and grandson of Varadayyaṅgār of Šrivatsa-gōtra, Āpastambha sūtra and Yajuś-śākha was to receive the entire village of Hāruvahalli as ēka-bhōgya and 32 of the 64 vyitis into which the other two villages were divided, the remaining 32 being distributed among Brāhmaṇas. The gift was made in the presence of god Gaṅgādharēśvara of Kakudgiri.

cells.date: Šaka 1494, Šubhakṛit, Bhādrapada śu. 12=1542 A.D., August 22. Tuesday. The solar eclipse occurred in the month of Šrāvaṇa, August 11, Friday.
cells.object: On a rock to the northeast of the village.

cells.date: Šaka 1265, Subhānu, Āvaṇi = 1343 A.D., July-August
cells.object: On the wall of the shrine of the goddess in the Varadarāja temple.
cells.remarks: Slightly damaged. It registers a grant made over to the stānattār and Chokkaperumāl-nādar, of the village Šipatipaṭti in Tēkka-nāđu as also the big lake constructed by Gōvinda-nāyakkar, and the wet and dry lands of the village by Periya Pemmaya-nāyakkar, son of Eṛamañchi Pemmaya-nāyakkar, for food-offierings, worship, lamp, gar lands, services and other offierings to god Aruļālanātha of Tēkkal. The nāṭṭavar of Tēkkal-nāđu undertook to carry out this sarvamānya endowment of the Šipatipalli village. It was attested by Sōmappaṇ, Sembiṇāyaṇ, Jayaṇā, aṇ and others.

cells.date: Śaka 1352, Sādhāraṇa, Māgha śu. 10, Thursday=1431 A.D., January 23, Tuesday.
cells.object: On a stone near the  mahādvāra  of the same temple.
cells.remarks: Records the grant or lands, horses and umbrellas to the carpenter Chōja Dēvoja, son of Bevõja of Tekal, and Añjala Liňgõja, the blacksmith for having done the wood and iron works (respectively) on the doors of the mukha-maṇṭapa and tower of Kalla Varadarāja temple using mango tree called Gaṇdabhēruṇda in Māragauḍanakaṭṭe, west of Mādanahalli in Pola-nāḍu. The gift was made by Siṅgarāja, son of Mallamarāja, the pradhāna of Gōparāja-vođeya, son of Sāļuva Tipparāja-vođeya. It also registers gifts of village, lands etc. to the temple officials, like the priests, attendants, cook, the śrivaishṇavas who recite, garland makers, songsters, dancers, the ūlīga servants etc., (named). The latter portion mentions Hiriya Hariyappa-vođeya, [Bu]karāya, Hariyapa-vođeya and Dēvarāya, The record falls in the reign-period of Dēvarāya II

cells.date: Śaka 1438, Pramādicha, Phālguṇa śu. 1, Thursday=1434 A.D., February 10, Wednesday. The Śaka year was 1356.
cells.object: On the  huli-baṇđe  west of the Varadarāja temple.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of Tēkal to Sāļuva Gōparāja, son of Sāļuva Tipparāja-vođeya, by Lak-kaṇṇa-vođeya and Mādaṇṇa-vođeya by the order of Dēvarāya-mahārāya. It also records the reconstruction, by pradhāna Siṅgarāja at the instance of Gōparāja and under orders from god Varadarāja of the inner and outer forts, originally built by Ballappa-daṇṇāyaka and Siṅgi-daṇṇāyaka, the ministers of Ballālarāya, but which was in ruins. It further records the erection of the bastion named Rājagambhira where Gōparāja and his son Tippaya hunted the tigers which were seized and brought by them.

cells.remarks: Damaged. cells.date: Śaka 1567 ( randhra-r'tu-bāṇa-chandra ), Pārthiva, Mārgaśirsha ba. 12 = 1645 A. D., December 4, Thursday
cells.remarks: A set of 3 copper-plates in the maṭha . Registers a gift of the village Chināṇikallu renamed Nārasimha in Kōlāla-dēśa by the king, to the pontiff Rāmachandra-bhārati, disciple of Viṭhala-bhārati, himself a disciple of Viśvarūpa-bhārati. Rāmakavi, son of Kāmakōṭi and grandson of Sabhāpati composed the record which was engraved by Sōmalātha, grandson of Gaṇapaya. The record contains a genealogical account of the king. It has the sign-manual Śrī Rāma at the end.

cells.date: Šaka 1266 ( rasa-rītu-nayana-indu ) Tāraṇa, Chaitra šu. 9=1344 A.D., March 23, Tuesday
cells.object: On copper plates of the village.
cells.remarks: Records a royal grant of the village Peñchakaladinna renamed Bukkarāyapura, in Penamāgaņi, in Kōđūru belonging to Guttiđurga-rājya, to Sōmanatha the great poet ( mahākavi ) son of illustrious Nāchana of Bhāradvāja-gōtra, Āpastambha-sūtra and Yajuś-śākha, who formed the village into 110 shares and retaining 26 for himself as the owner's ( yajāmāea ) share bestowed the others on various Brāhmaṇas, named. But the details given account only for 80 vṛittis . The record gives a genealogical account and states that in the family of Yadu was born Bukka who had a wife named Mamgāmoikā and in this latter's family was born Saṅgama who had five sons from Mālām̂bikā—Harihara, Kampa, Bukka, Mārapa and Muddapa. The middle (third) son who succeeded Harihara made this grant. The donee is described as a poet in 8 languages. The king is stated to have been ruling from Vidyānagari established ( kṛitā ) by Vidyāraṇya. The record, composed by Mallaṇārādhya son of Kōṭidēvārādhyāchārya , was engraved by the sculptor ( śilpi ) Nāgidēva.

cells.date: Śaka 1339, Durmukhi, Mārgaśira śu. 10=1416 A.D., November 30, Monday, the Śaka year being current.
cells.remarks: Boulder leaning to the temple of Nāchāramma. States that Annadāni-vođeya was administering Muļuvāgila-rājya belonging to (the chief-taincy of) mahāpradhāna Nāgaṇṇa-vođeya, under the orders of Nāchidēvi, the mūlasthāna goddess of Muļuvāyi, the śthānikas Kēšava-perumāl, his sons Balepa, Maṇiya and Mārapa and his younger brother Aubhaļa, of the (temple of) Nāchidēvi gave a charter to the mahājanas of Muļuvayi headed by Šivarātreya Viṭhaṇṇa and Mallanṇa, sons of Dēvarasa. The irrigational dam called Araṭiyaāne over the river Pālār in Katariyahaļiya-sime belonging to the goddess having broken since long, the mahājanas got it repaired at a great cost borne by themselves and also established a village named Muļuvāya Nāchipura. In lieu of this the temple authorities now made them a gift of the village Yalachi-yakuṇte and uncultivated lands besides forests which the mahājanas were to clean for cultivation. The yield from this was to be divided into 4 shares one of which was to be made over to the temple treasury, the other three being enjoyed by themselves. They were also granted the village Muļuvāyi Nāchipura which was converted into a sarvamānya agrahāra . It cites the sthānikas as signatories.

cells.date: Šaka 1353, Sādhāraṇa, Phālguṇa śu. 10 = 1431 A.D., February 10, Wednesday. The Šaka year was current.
cells.object: On a copper-plate in possession of Sāyar Krishnappa.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of six villages (1) Gutṭehaļli, (2) Sūrādēvihaļli, (3) Mahādēvanahaļli, (4) Virūpākshapura, (5) Kumudēvanahaļli, (6) Kuṁchibaṇdētaraphu in Muļuvāyi-sime for celebrating daily, fortnightly, and monthly festivals and car festivals of god Prasanna Virūpāksha, by Lakhaṇṇa-daṇṇāyaka and MāJaṇṇadaṇṇāyaka, sons of Vommāyamma and Heggađedēva of Vishṇuvardhana-gōtra. It also records the construction of towers and enclosures, excavation of a tank named Manmatha-pushkaraṇi, etc. for the temple, at the instance of Vijayarāya. On the given date Dēvarāya II was ruling.

cells.date: Śaka 1389, Sarvajit, Māgha ba. 14, Śivarātri=1468 A.D., February 7 Sunday. A lunar eclipse occurred on that day, f.d.t. .31
cells.object: On the south wall of the Sōmēśvara temple of Sōmēśvarapālya.
cells.remarks: Records exemption from several taxes like gavuḍa-suṅka , tax on looms, talāvāḥike , tribute, kaḍḍāya , biḍagoḥu (levy on camps new and old) and (merchandise on) two bullock-loads to Yeleya Saṅkappa-seṭṭi, son of baṇajiga Daṇḍappa, of Muḥuvāya-paṭṭaṇa, in lieu of which he was to supply 2 betel leaves to be offered daily to god Sōmēyadēva of Muḥuvāyi. It refers to two paṇas of siddhāya which was also probably exempted from payment. The grant was made by Hariyappa of Muḥuvāyi for the merit of Narasiṅgarāja-oḍeya.

cells.date: Śaka 1440, Bahudhānya, Vaiśākha śu. 15=1518 A.D., April 25, Sunday
cells.object: On the stone in the south wall of the Sōmēśvara temple at Sōmēśvarapālya.

cells.date: Śaka 1.90, Ēśvara, Kārttika śu. 15, Thursday, Rōhiṇi. The details are irregular. The Śaka year would be either 1499 or 1559, when in the cyclic year cited the  tithi  occurred on Saturday, October 26, of 1577 A.D., or Monday, October 23 of 1637 A.D., the  nakshatra  on both the days being Bharaṇi. In the Śaka year 1490 (Vibhava) the  tithi  occurred on Thursday, 1568 A.D., November 4—a date too early for Veñkaṭapati I.
cells.object: On a copper-plate in the Śrīpādarāya-maṭha.
cells.remarks: . . . ., Vijaya Veñkaṭapatirāya Records a royal grant of the village Veñgere along with its hamlets situated in the Vađaga Rātūra-hōbaļi attached to Paramati-sthaļa, belonging to the westein fort of the Vūṭakūru-simhāsana to the Muļabāgilu-maṭha, for worship and offerings to god Gōpinātha. The recipient of the gift was the pontiff Suvarṇavarṇa Paraśurāma-tirtha, disciple of Sañkar-shaṇa-tirtha, himself a disciple of Ādi(Vādi ?) rāja-tirtha-śripāda. The king is said to be the grandson of Narasimharāya and son of Virupāksharāya. The record appears to be spurious. There is no king of that name who was the grandson of Narasimharāya, and son of Virūpāksha.

cells.date: Šaka 1453, Khara, Āsvija šu. 13 =1531 A.D., September 24, Sunday.
cells.remarks: Two faces of a stone in a bush to the east of the village. Slightly damaged. Records the grant of the village Basavāpaťťana in Manđibale-sthala of Nallūru-sime as an umbaļi to Timmappa, son of Bairapa-gauđa of Vēlūru. The grant was made by [Garbhasaru ?] mahāpātre , the agent of Sōmasilāgihu (?) Rāūttarāya-mahāpātre. The gift appears to have been made for conducting a weekly fair ( sante ). The record refers to it as samtigiya umbaļi-māni .

cells.date: Šaka 1300, Kāļayukti, Šrāvaņa ba. 12, Friday =1378 A.D., August 20
cells.object: On a stone south of the Rāmēšvara temple.
cells.remarks: Dēpaņna-vođeya, son of Khantikāx arāyara-gaņda Nāgaņna-vcđeya is stated to be administering Sādaliya-nāđu when a fair ( samthe ) was established in the village Rāmēšvara after consulting Kanna-gauđa, the nāđagauđa of Sādali, and other gauđas including Bayappa of Rāmēšvara, the Five seṭṭis of Sere, all the elders ( halaru ) of the sālumūle who all sat in an assembly for this purpose. It was laid down that no tax was to be levied in the first year where after taxes ( āya ) at the rate of 1 towards rājāya , 1 towards nāthāya , 1 for the (body of) Five seṭṭis ( ayvaru seṭṭaru ) and 1 for the minđaguđđas was to be collected.

cells.date: Śaka 1254, Angirasa, Vaiśākha ba. 30, solar eclipse. These details are irregular. The Śaka year (1332-33 A.D.) is too early. In Śaka 1374, the  tithi  fell on 1452 A.D., May 19, Friday. But, there was no eclipse on that day. Mallikārjuna was the ruling king.
cells.object: On a set of 3 copper-plates.
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of the village Mallasamudra in Buruḍukunṭa-sthala in Mukkoṇḍa-vēṇthe of Sādali-pīṭha to Chokkaṇṇa-bhaṭṭa-jōsya, son of Śriraṅga-bhaṭṭa and grandson of Chakravarti-bhaṭṭa, belonging to Śrivatsa-gōtra, Āpastambha-sūtra and.Yajuś-śakha by Timmarāju, son of Yara Timmarāju and grandson of Nalla Timmarāju of Ātrēya-gōtra, in the presence of the king and of god Virūpāksha. The given date is too early for the king, who is said to be the son of Vijaya-bhūpati and Nārāyaṇām'bikā. The record does not appear to be genuine.

cells.date: Śaka 1318, Yuva, Āśvayuja śu. 10, Thursday=1395 A.D., September 24, Friday. The Śaka year was current.
cells.object: On a stone near the Veñkaṭaramaṇa temple, south of the village.
cells.remarks: Records the setting up of a lamp post ( dipamāle )(in front of the temple of)god Vighnēśvara by Mārappana Chinnaṇṇa, son of Mācha-gaunḍa, who was administering Hodali village in Bilusōṇi-nāḍu of Muļuvāyi-rājya for the merit of his parents. The grant was made when Bukkarāya (II) was ruling the Muļuvāyi kingdom. Kaṭtigeya Nāgappa, Tiṇṇala Chikkappa, the prabhu of Bilusōṇa, nāḍu, rendered assistance in this work of charity. The stone was written (engraved?) by Piṇgaṇa, son of Piṇgaṇa.

cells.remarks: Byāladakere Records the renewal of a grant by the king of the village Belekere renamed Vira Nārasimhēndrapura, in Śindaghaṭṭa-sime of Hoyisaṇa-dēśa, to Śrīnivāsa, son of Subra'hmaṇya, a resident of Śriraṅgapaṭṭaṇa. The original grant had been made to Subrahmaṇya (the father of the donee) for his individual enjoyment ( ēkabhōga ) by Vira Narasimha, in the year Vibhava, Vaiśākha śu. 12 (1508 A.D., April 12), at Śriśaila, on the occasion of his performing saptasāgara dāna . The record, composed by Sabhāpati, was engraved by Viraṇāchārya son of Mallaṇa.

cells.date: Šaka 1383, Chitrabhānu, Māgha ba. 14, Sunday, Šravaṇa-nakshatra, Šivaiātri. Irregular. In the given Šaka year details correspond to 1462 A.D., January 29, Friday, Šravaṇa, the cyclic year being Vṛisha. In Chitrabhānu (Šaka 1384) the  tithi  occurred on 1463A.D. February 17, Thursday, Dhanishṭha. In either case, the date is too early for the king.
cells.reference: EC., VI (Rev. 1977) Kr. 71; XIV (1 edn.), Kr. 99
cells.object: Copper-plate in the possession of a resident of the village.
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of the village Kaigoṇdapalli alias Vira Narasimhapura, in Sindhughaṭta-sime of Hoyisaļa-dēša, to Nañje-hebbāruva of Atri-gōtra and Drāhyāyaṇa-sūtra, by the king on the occasion of his performing saptasāgaradāna in the presence of god Šiva a Sriśaila. The record contains the eulogy usually associated with Kṛishpadēvarāya. The date given is too early for any member of the Tuļuva family that ruled over Vijayanagara. The genuineness of the record is not beyond doubt.

cells.date: Šaka 1304, Durmati, Dvitiya-Vaisākha ba. 5, Monday=1381 A.D., May 13, Monday, f.d.t., Šaka year was current.
cells.object: On a stone to the left of the Viraguđi temple.
cells.remarks: Records the death of Bhaṭtara Bachiyappa, son of Kirtirāja and states that the deceased had Bukkarāya-samudra, Kīrti-samudra. Mālūvveyakeře, Nāgavveyakeře, Bachappanakeře and Chauđappa's channel excavated, raised an areca garden at Bāchipaṭṭaṇa and also installed god Mallikārjuna. The obsequies were performed by the deceased's son. Bukkaṇṇa, at Virūpāksha (Hampe). The record was composed by Nřisimha. A post-script added much later states that Kampaṇṇa-vođeya died in the year Plava, Vaisākha ba. 6, (Saturday).

cells.date: [Vi]bhāva, Chaitra śu. 1, Monday=1388 A.D., March 9
cells.object: On a stone east of the Siddhēdēva temple.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Registers a gift of the village Boppa-samudra, hamlet of Hādariyavāgilu and certain lands on rent to Bukkaṇṇa, Kampaṇṇa and Chauḍappa, sons of Bhaṭara Bāchiyappa who bears several epithets. The rent was 40 varāhas per year. They were exempted from taxes like beḍu, binugu, daļamiļi, grāmagadyāṇa, nibandhi, nallettu, nallemme, koṭtage etc. The purpose of the grant was to conduct festivals to the gods of Boppa-samudra and for the gauḍike of the place. Sēnabōva Bommaṇṇa wrote the record.

cells.date: Śaka 1314, Āmgirasa, Āšvayuja śu. 1, Sunday=1392 A.D., September 18
cells.object: On a stone, east of the Māri-guđi.
cells.remarks: The language of the record is somewhat unintelligible. It refers to Bukkaṇṇa, son of Bhaṭṭara Bāchiyappa of Aruhanahaļļi, belonging to Bađavāra family, Dēvappa, son of Sāya-nāyaka of Hādaravāgilu belonging to Tiļlara family and Rāmappa and Allappa, sons of Dēvana-nāyáka (same as Dēvappa ?) who appear to have made over varaha-guļige-ga to Kirtidēva, Kampaṇṇa and Chavuđappa, probably as a loan. Several individuals are cited as witnesses. Mallitamma, son of Chaūđōja, the sēnabōva , appears to have written the record.

cells.date: Śaka 1544, Dundubhi, Māgha śu. 10=1623 A.D., January 31

cells.date: Šaka 1396 ( rtu, randhra, guņa, vidhu ), Vijaya, Pushya šu. 10, Āmģirasa-vāra (Thursday) Makara-samkrānti = 1473 A.D., December 28, Tuesday
cells.object: On a set of 5 copper-plates in the possession of Taļavāra Timma.
cells.remarks: Sanskrīt in Nāgari This record contains a genealogical account of the dynasty and states that Virūpāksha was the son of Pratāparāya and Simhaladēvi and grandson of Vijaya and Nārāyaņi. The first part registers a gift of the village Ālugōđu on the Kāvēri, with its hamlet Nuggilūru to several Brāhmaņas, in the presence of god Virūpāksha. Thereafter it is stated that upon the request of Dēpaya of the family of mahāmaņđalēšvara Haryaņa, the same villages were gifted to Krīshņa-bhaťta who divided the same into several vrittis and distributed them among Brāhmaņas Dugnapa, son of Mādhavārādhya, the composer. Vallabha, son of Aitapārya, the writer and Mallana, son of Viraņa, the scribe also got one vritti each. 139 :

cells.remarks: Set of 3 copper-plates in the possession of M.A. Srinivasacharya, Advocate. Records a royal grant of the village Maṇtheya, renamed Krīshṇarāyapūra, along with its hamlets in Šriraṅga paṭṭaṇa-sīme, of Hoysaļa-dēśa, to his pontiff Gōvindarāja, son of Varadāchārya of Bhāradvāja-gōtra, Āpasthambha-sūtra and Yajuś-śākha, at the time of the king's performing ghrīta-parvvata-dāna . The donee is said to have belonged to the family of Anantāchārya whom god Veňkatēśa appears to have honoured with a garland. The hamlets granted were Chikka Maṇteya, Kallahaļli, Hosahaļli, Taṇđasēhaļli and Kōnēhaļli. The record, composed by Sabhāpati, was engraved by Mallaṇāchārya.

cells.remarks: Purports to register a grant of lands in the village Muttegere in Nāgamaṅgala-stha ļa of Hai(Hoy)sala-nāđu, by Rāṇā Pedda Jagadēvarāya, as amara to Dele-gauđa (of Šivāchāra), Naļamāra, Hūchchamāra and another. The language and orthography are very faulty. The date is to early (by centuries !). Evidently a forgery.

The grant was made in the presence of god Gaṅgādhara of Śivagaṅga. It is said that the donee divided that village into 20 vṛittis and granted them to several Brāhmaṇas. Record was composed by the poet Sabhāpati and engraved by Mallanāchārya, son of Vīraṇāchārya.

cells.date: Šaka 1380 (also expressed by the chronogram  Khāba-rāmēndu ), Bahudhānya, Mārgaśira ba. 12, Šaurivāra =1453 A.D., December 2, Saturday
cells.object: Stone set up to the right of the verandah in the Jiyar temple.
cells.remarks: Refers to the predecessors of the king commencing from Samgama ; but does not mention Harihara 1 and Bukka 11. Records construction of the Raṅga-maṭha by Raṅgāmbikāe wife of Timmaṇna-daṇṇāyaka, on a deserted site purchased by her. She is said to have offered several gifts to god Nārāyaṇa of Mēlugōte in the form of jewels, silver palanquins, maṇtapa and tank. She desired that 24 devoted vaishṇavas should be fed in the Raṅga-maṭha whereupon, her husband appealed to the king and having received from him through a copper-plate grant, made a gift of the villages Bālēnahaļli and Yalavadahaļli, the hamlets of Mēlugōte in Kuruvańka-nāđa-vēṇṭheya of Hoysaļa-rājya. The lands below Raṅga-samudra which had earlier been donated to god Chelapilērāya were exempted. Since the income of 80 varahas raised was found to be insufficient, more land yielding an income of 40 varahas was purchased by him for 400 varahas and made over to Rāmānuja-jiya who was to maintain the grant and look after the the maṭha by staying there itself. Timmaṇṇa-daṇṇāyaka was the son of Śingaṇṇa of Lōhita family, the mahāprabhu of Nāgamaṅgala and Sitāmbikā.

cells.remarks: Registers a gift of houses and sites in Nalanahalī, a hamlet of Kuļiyakeķe and Kurukulavampāđi, all situated in Saṇabi Mukuļiya-nāđu and lands below the tank Parāṅkuśa-samudra, to a number of śri vaishṇavas (named) who were serving the ālṣvār at Kurukulavampāđi. by Nāchiyāramma, a devotee of god Nārāyaṇa, goddesss Lakshmīdēvi and ascetic Śaṭhagōpa. at the instance of mahāpradhāna Timmaṇṇa-daṇṇāyaka and the Fiftytwo Vaishṇavas of the Nārāyaṇa temple of Tirunārāyaṇapura. The language of the record is not quite clear. Rāmanuja wrote the record.

cells.date: Śaka 1449, Sarvajit, Māgha śu. 7=1528 A.D., January 28, Tuesday.
cells.reference: EC., VI (Rev. 1977), Pp. 134; XIV (1 edn.) Sr. 263
cells.object: On the lawer part of the wall to the north of the same  prākāra .
cells.remarks: By the order of the king, Krīshṇarāya-nāyaka, son of Daṇđu Avubhaļadēva made a grant of the villages Kāmanāyakanahalļi and Gollara Chaṭṭanahalļi situated in Śrīraṅgapaṭṭaṇa and Sindegaṭṭa śimes respectively, yielding an annual income of 105 gadyāṇas , and income from several taxes like santheya āya (tax on weekly fair) of Mēlugōte, taļavāḥike of Sindaghaṭṭa, hogede ře , sthaļa-suṇika , customs on betel nuts, āđade ře and rāyasta-varītane -all these yielding 149 gadyāṇas , the total income being 254 gadyāṇas . The gift was made on the rathasaptami day, on the bank of the Kāvērī, to the temple of Nārāyaṇa, for the mer it of the king. It is further recorded that since, formerly, the cultivators of the temple lands were being carried off to Tonđanūru for ploughing the lands there, those lands also have now been granted. Sēnabōva Rāmānuja wrote the record.

Pērirāja, son of Harigila Abbarāja had repaired the tanks named Hosakere and Krīshṇa-dēvavođeyarakeře at a cost of 150 gadyaṇas whereupon, the Fiftytwo Ayyas of the temple initiated a charity in his name according to which offerings were to be made to the deity from the temple treasury. One quarter of the same was to be made over to Pērirāja or his nominee. The charity was to continue even if the tank breached at a later date.

cells.date: Šaka 1457, Manmatha, Āshāḥha śu. 11=1535 A.D., June 11, Friday.
cells.reference: EC., VI (Rev. 1977), PP. 125; III, XIV (1 edn.), Sr. 95
cells.remarks: Basement stone of the north wall of the same temple. Registers a grant of the villages Seṭipura and Mālanahalī and their hamlets Nilamaṅgala, Hoļava||i and Karanāranahalī, made over to the treasury of god Chelapiļarāya, also known as Sampatkara Nārāyaṇa of Yādavagiri alias Tirunārāyaṇapura, after getting those villages released from Rāmā-bhaṭṭa who had originally received it through a copper-plate grant. The gift was made by Tirumalarāja, son of Harinila Abbarāja, described as Maṇi-nāgapuravarādhīṣvara , for food-offerings daily and during the raft ( teppa ) festival conducted in the newly constructed tank. It is specified that a portion (one taļige ) of offerings was to be given to Varadāchārya of Peraṅgūru, described as madya-sudarśanāchārya . The Fiftytwo of the sthāna are stated to have agreed for the grant.

cells.date: Śaka 1466, Krōdhi, Kārttika śu. 12=1544 A.D., October 27, Monday.
cells.reference: EC., VI (Rev. 1977), PP. 130; XIV (I edn.), Sr. 259
cells.remarks: Second stone in the same prākāra . This is a charter of charity given by Nārayadēva, son of Narasiṅgadēva of Nandyāla, to the ascetic Vēdānti Rāmānuja-jiya, discipline of Kandāđi Aṇṇa of Śrīraṅga. Although the exact import is not clear, it appears to state that the seal, called dēśāntri-mudre , of the temple of Chalapiļerāya of Mēlugōṭe alias Tirunārāyaṇapura, originally given by Achyutarāya of Dēvagiri (Vijayanagara ?) had now been allowed by the chief to be used by the Yatirāja-maṭha where, once śri Bhāshyakāra, i.e. Rāmānujāchārya, had taken his residence. As a consequence, the pontiff of the maṭha became entitled for a share in the temple property and was permitted to use the seal called Hanumanta-mudre as also the Rāmānuja-mudre besides the royal seal. He was also to receive all honours as the Fiftytwo yatis . The donor had received Śrīraṅgapaṭṭaṇa-sīme for his chieftaincy. Sēnabōya Rāmānuja wrote the record with the consent of the Fiftytwo.

cells.remarks: Records a grant of the village Ballālapura in Śriraṅgapaṭṭaṇa-sīme and Varāhana Kala-hall in Molanāđa-sthaļa of Kaṇambāđi-sīme for several services in the temple of god Chelapiļerāya of Yādavagiri alias Tirunārāyaṇapura by mahāmaṇđalēšvara Nārāyadēva-mahā-arasu of Nandyāla, belonging to Ātrēya-gōtra, Āpastambha-sūtra and Yajuś-śākha. cells.date: Šaka 1473, Virōdhakīit, Āšvayuja ba. 10=1551.A.D., October 24, Saturday.
cells.reference: EC., VI (Rev. 1977), PP. 131; XIV (I edn.), Sr. 260
cells.object: On the wall to the west in the same  prakāra .
cells.remarks: Registers a grant of a village Nagulanahalli to god Sampatkara Nārāyaṇa alias Chelapiļerāya of Yādavagiri alias Tirunārāyaṇapura by Appayyaṅgār, son of Embāraya and mahāmaṇdalēśvara Timmeyadēva-mahā-arasu, son of Narasiṅgadēva-mahā-arasu of Nandyāla. It states that earlier Virama-nāyaka had gifted that village to Embārayya, but it was taken back by Kṛishṇaraya. Embārayya's son, Appayyaṅgār got back half the village when he presented a golden garuḍa to the temple. The gift was made for worship, offering several dishes, etc. in the shrine of Varāhasvāmi, maintaining the flower garden etc. Appayyaṅgar was to get 1/4 of the offerings made. Sēnabōva Rāmānuja wrote the record.

cells.date: Śaka 1486, Raktākshi, Mārgaśira ba. 10=1564 A.D., November 28, Tuesday.
cells.reference: EC., VI (Rev. 1977), PP. 128; XIV (1 edn.), Sr. 257
cells.remarks: To the left of entrance in the same prākāra . Records the grant of two villages, Hoṅganūru belonging to Channapaṭṭaṇa-sthala and Honnuḍage belonging to Gūlūru-sthala, along with their hamlets, for the car-festival, conducting special service during the 12 natal star days of Bhāshyakāra, i.e. , Rāmānujāchārya, and on the natal star days of Chūḍikuḍutta-nāchiyār and Periya-jiya, as also for maintaining the flower garden, the Rāmānuja-kūṭa and for other services in the temple of god Sampatkara Nārāyaṇa alias Cheluvapillerāya at Yādavagiri alias Tirunārāyaṇapura, by mahāmaṇdalēśvara Koṇḍarājayadēva-mahā-arasu, son of Kōnēṭirājudēva-mahā-arasu and grandson of Hiri Koṇḍarājadēva-mahā-arasu of Ātrēya-gōtra and Āpastambha-sūtra. The gift villages had been received by the donor for amaranāyakatana , by the king, through a copperplate charter. Rāmānuja, the sēnabōva of the temple treasury, wrote the record.

cells.date: Śaka 1492, Pramōdūta, Chaitra śu. 2=1570 A.D., March 8, Wednesday.
cells.reference: EC., VI (Rev. 1977), PP. 132 ; XIV (1 edn.), Sr. 261
cells.object: On the same wall.
cells.remarks: States that earlier Vasantarāya of Velugōđu family had sold the village Mailanaha||i a hamlet of Mēlukōṭe and another hamlet (name lost), to the temple and had placed Anantayya as the dharmakarta , to look after the offerings in the Rāmānuja-kūṭa and service of god Nārāyapa. But this gift had become defunct. Thereupon, Rāyapa-nāyaka, son of Chitrako-nṇama-nāyaka of Velugōđu renewed the same grant after consulting Jaleļa Raṅgapatirājayya and made an agreement with the Fiftytwo ayyas of Yādavagiri. Āļvāru Siņgaya, grandson of Anantayya, was appointed as the dharmakarta to look after the renewed endowment. Sēnabōva Rāmānuja wrote the record.

cells.date: 1. Pārthiva, Śrāvaṇa ba. 8, Saturday, Rōhiṇi,  śrijayanti =1455 A.D., August 14, Wednesday.
cells.reference: EC., VI (Rev. 1977). PP. 19; III (1 edn.) Sr. 139
cells.object: On two stones in a field.
cells.remarks: 2. Śaka 1390, Sarvajit, Prathama Bhādrapada ba. 8, Saturday, Rōhiṇi=1467 A.D., August 22, Saturday. Dēvarāja, son of Šiņgaņa-vođeya of Nāgamaņgala had dug out from the Kāvēri a channel which the mahājanas of Harahu desired to be extended to their village boundary also, in lieu of which they were to give him the yajāmāna-bhāga . He had received the village Hosaha!li in Kuruvańkanāđa-vēņthe from Yaduvaņna, son of hebāruva Širaņganātha as śrotriya . Later, on the second date of the record, Yaduvaņna sold the villages Chikka-maļali, Hosaha!li and half portion of Kendanahāļu, for a sum of 400 hons . Dēvarāja divided lands of the village Hosaha!li so purchased by him into 208 vrittis and distributed them among the 78 mahājanas and also made a gift to the temple of god Rāmachandra for the merit of his mother Sitāyamma. The record was written by Kođavagiya.

cells.date: Śaka 1464, Raktākshi, Āshāḥha śu. 12. Irregular. Cyclic year=Śaka 1486 when the  tithi  occurred on 1564 A.D., June 21. But by then Achyutarāya was not ruling at all.
cells.reference: EC., VI (Rev. 1977), Sr. 5 ; III (I edn.), Sr. 6
cells.object: On a stone near the  bṛindāvana , north of outer  prākāra  of the Raṅganatha temple.
cells.remarks: During his management Kāmappa-nāyaka had collected taxes amounting to 300 gadyāṇas which had not been prevalent till then, from rent-free villages and revenue villages in the đalāvayi-agrahāras of Śrīraṅgapaṭṭaṇa as also from feeding houses and temples. These had now been exempted by Peddirāja, son of Appāji of Kāśyapa-gōtra who had been assigned the māgaṇi of the said sime by Rāmābhaṭṭayya. Also the ālaya-suṁka (house tax ?) of Hāruvaha!li and Vogeya-samudra from Peraṅgūr-ayya had been exempted. The gift was made to the mahājanas who were not to pay any other tax beyond 3 haṇas towards volāvāru to the merchants ( baṇajigas ) who purchased betelnuts from them. The gift was made for the merit of the king and Rāmābhaṭṭayya.

cells.date: Šaka 1477, Rākshasa, Šrāvaṇa ba. 8=1555 A.D., August 9, Friday.

cells.object: On a stone set up to the west of the village.

Raṅgarajavya wrote the record which ends with the sign-manual śri Kṛishṇa

cells.date: Šaka 1485, Rudirōdgāri, Šrāvaṇa ba. 10=1563 A.D., August 13, Friday
cells.object: Slab set up in front of the Māri-guđi.
cells.remarks: When Sadāśivarāya was ruling, Timmappa-nāyaka, son of Māyappa-nāyaka of Kovuttūr granted the village Bānagavāđi in Ghaleyada-sthala, free of tax and with all the rights, to Mādēva, pontiff of the Viraśaiva maṭha named Upparig-ya-maṭha in Ummattūru, for the smerit of his parents. The donor was the chief ( nāyaka ) of Ghaleyada-sthala. The gift is said to have been made in ardhōdaya which occurred on January 24, 1563 A.D. (Pushyaamāvāsye, Šrāvapa-nakshatra, Sunday). Therefore, the record appears to have been set up nearly six months later.

cells.date: Śaka 1527, Viśvāvasu, Vaiśākha śu. 3=1605 A.D., April 11, Thursday
cells.reference: EC., IV (Rev. 1975), Ch. 1; IV (1 edn.), Ch. 82
cells.object: Stone on the pial to the left of the main entrance of the Virabhadra temple.
cells.remarks: It states that till the date of the record the village Haṅgaṛapura, situated in Uyyamba!li-sthala of Ummattūru-sime was being enjoyed as śrōtriya-guttige by the vođeyas of Kamarava!li and that the rental amount was being paid to the chief ( prabhu ) of Arekoṭhāra. Now, after mutual understanding between Chandraśēkhara-vođeya, son of Channarāja-vođeya, the chief of Arekoṭhāra-sthala and Malarāja-vođeya, son of Vira Rāmaya-vođeya of Kammarava!li, the village was made over to god Virabhadradēva of Arekoṭhāra as a sarvamānya for offerings to god and the maintenance of dancing girls in the temple ( pātrabhōga ). The signatory of the record is Mallarāja.

cells.remarks: It refers to the rule of Veňkaťapatirāya (I) described as mahāmaṇḍalēśvara , and registers a gift of the village Channappanapura, for worship, offerings, etc., of the deities Kumbhēśvara. cells.date: Akshaya, Pushya ba. 1. The record may be assigned to c. 14th century, when the given year occurred in 1386-87 A.D. The details are insufficient for verification. But they correspond to 1387 A.D., January 5, Saturday, f.d.t. .17.
cells.object: On a stone in a garden to the north of the village.
cells.remarks: This inscription refers to mahāmaṇdalēšvara Vira Hariyappa-vođeya and states that Mūd-aṇṇa-ođeya made a grant of an arecanut-garden and wet land, below the tank called Kōvegere, to god Bhōganātha. cells.date: Śaka 1290, Kilaka, Vaiśākha, ba. 5, Monday, Śravaṇa-nakshatra=1368 A.D., May 8, Sunday
cells.object: On a second stone set up in the same place.
cells.remarks: It refers to the rule of Vira Bukkaṇṇa-vođeya (1) and to his minister Basavayya-daṇṇāyaka. The latter's subordinate Gaṇapa Tima (?) is said to be administering the Hoysaļa country to the south of the river Kāvēri. It registers a grat of lands etc., in Mātrihaļli, besides income from kuļa , baļi and binugude xe to god Aṇilēśvara of Haradanahaļli, for worship and offerings, by all the gauđas of Uyyamapaļli, described as the first village ( prathama-sthaļa ) of Yeṇne-nāđu, the mahājanas of Kēśavapura also called Nagara and several gauđas etc., of Haradanahaļli, Amachavāđi etc.

The latter's subordinate Gaṇapa Tima (?) is said to be administering the Hoysaļa country to the south of the river Kāvēri. It registers a grat of lands etc., in Mātrihaļli, besides income from  kuļa ,  baļi  and  binugude xe  to god Aṇilēśvara of Haradanahaļli, for worship and offerings, by all the  gauđas  of Uyyamapaļli, described as the first village ( prathama-sthaļa ) of Yeṇne-nāđu, the  mahājanas  of Kēśavapura also called Nagara and several  gauđas  etc., of Haradanahaļli, Amachavāđi etc.

cells.king: Chikka Kam[paṇṇa], son of Bukka I (?)
cells.object: Stone in a wet land to the west of Āñjanēya temple.
cells.remarks: Jyēshṭha ba. 1, Saturday (?). Details cannot be verified. The record, on paleographical grounds, may be assigned to the 14th century. Broken. Appears to contain an instruction issued by Chikka Kam[paṇṇa-vođeya] to the tax-collectors and officers to collect the taxes and fines due from the people of Hadināđu. Officers of Haṭṭalakōṭe are referred to. Chikka Kampaṇṇa may be the son of Bukka I. He figures in other records of the region.

cells.date: Śaka 1445, Svabhānu, Śrāvaṇa ba. 10, Thursday=1523 A.D., August 6
cells.reference: EC., IV (Rev. 1975), Ch. 224; IV (I edn.), Ch. 99
cells.object: Stone to the south of Virabhadra temple.
cells.remarks: During the rule of Křishṇarāya-mahārāya of Vijayanagara, Jađeyāru-modaliyār, son of Tiruvēṅgađa-modaliyar of Tuřumuđipāka, an officer ( māgaṇikāṭa ) under the minister Sāļuva Gövindarāja, consecrated god Virabhadra in Haṭṭalakōṭe, within his māgaṇi and granted lands in Surigehaļa, Kađeyaghaṭṭa, Maruhaļi, Hebbasūru, etc., to provide for its worship. The recipient of this gift as also the future gifts that may be made, was Allappa who was designated as the karta of the sthāna and was made responsible for regular worship etc., in the temple. A supplement at the end seems to register a grant of a shop (?— santeya pasarāya aṅgađi ).

cells.date: Śaka 1302, Raudri, Šrāvaṇa śu. 5, Sunday=1380 A.D., July 7, Saturday.
cells.object: On a stone set up in front of the Mūlasthānēšvara temple.
cells.remarks: This record gives the genealogy of Hariyappa-vođeya (Harihara 11), the Vijayanagara king, who is said to be the son of Bukka 1 and grandson of Saṅgama and Kāmāyi. Hari-hara's minister was Kampa at whose instance Ballappa, son of Saṅgamarāja, was governing Hadināđu, Then it describes the village Homma alias Akaļańka-chaturvēđimaṅgala, also called Sarvajña Vishṇupura. For the worship, offerings etc., to god Mūlasthānadēva (temple situated at the eastern gateway) of this place, a gift of land was made by the mahājanas of the 108 vṛittis , made over to Bhūtāṇđihāruva, the sthānika of the temple. The mahājanas have been described as well-versed in logic, grammar, prosody and fine arts like dancing. Some of them are named, as Aļagha-perumāļ of Pulkūru, Koṇđāru of Dēsa-maṅgala, Allāļanāthā of Kuṛuhaṭṭi, Kēśāva of Vaṅgipura. The epigraph was written by Aksharada Gōpaṇṇa.

cells.date: Yuva (Yīva), Pushya šu. 5. Probably=1515  A.D. , December 10, Monday
cells.reference: EC., IV (Rev. 1975), Ch. 162; IV (I edn.), Ch. 39
cells.object: On a stone set up to the north of Mārī-chāvađi.
cells.remarks: Slightly damaged. Refers to Sāļuva Gōvindarājayya, obviously the officer under Křishņa-dēvarāya States that 10 amkaņas of house-site belonging to Dođaņa-seťti, were taken over for the palace, in lieu of which house-site of the same size was given to him elsewhere. along with a sealed letter ( kempottida völe ). It appears that this latter site had been made over to the palace by Naňjadēpa who could not pay the kuļasthe (tax ?). The transaction was made at the instance of Sāļuva Gōvindarājayya by his pārupatyagāra whose name is lost.

cells.date: Šaka 1347, Višvāvasu. Jyēshṭha ba. 11, Tuesday=1425 A.D., June 12
cells.reference: EC., IV (Rev. 1975), Ch. 308; IV (I edn.), Ch. 195
cells.object: On a stone to the west of Māri-chāvađi.
cells.remarks: Registers an interesting episode of Hariyaṇṇā, son of Huliyara Hāyaṇṇa, stopping the horse called Parvatinātha which jumped into the valley (or river ?) scared as it was by seeing a boar. Mahāmaṇdalēšvara Vira Pārvatirāya-ođeya, son (?) of king Vira Vijayarāya, who was administering Terakaṇambi-rājya was, at that time, riding on that horse in the hunting ground to the east of the hill of Tirumalanātha. The record is described as a jaya-stambha , set up in memory of this event.

cells.date: Śaka 1344, Šubhakṛit, Śrāvaṇa śu. 15, Sunday, lunar eclspse=1422 A.D., August 2.
cells.reference: EC., IV (Rev. 1975), Ch. 372; IV (I edn.), Ch. 159
cells.object: Copper-plate record in the Pārśvanātha basadi.
cells.remarks: This record, engraved on a set of three copper-plates, registers a grant of the village Maleyūr and its hamlet Huṇusūrapura, together with all lands and incomes from taxes like ađadere, kumbaradeř (tax on potters), kallamana, binugu, sumka at the rate of hāga per hon, daňnāyakara-svāmya , etc., pertaining thereto to god Vijayanātha of Kanakagiri by kumāra Harihararāya-vođeya (Harihara III), son of Děvarāya II of Vijayanagara, in the presence of god Triyambaka. The gift was exclusive of the paddy land under the tank in front of the village formerly granted to god Vāsuděva of Kolagaṇa. The gift villages are said to be in Kolagaṇa of Terakaṇāmbe-rājya which was being administered by the prince.

text.remarks: Registers the gift of the village Da nāyakanapura in Uyyambali-sthaļa for the services of god Nañjuṇđeśvara and feeding of six Brāhmaṇas daily, by Perumāle-adhikāri at the instante of Achyutarāya, the king. Dēvēšā-bhaṭa appears to be the recipient of the gift.

cells.date: Śaka 1351, Samaya (Saumya), Chaitra śu. 15=1429 A.D., March 20, Sunday. There occurred a lunar eclipse on that day.
cells.object: Stone set up in a field to the north.
cells.remarks: This damaged epigraph records the gift of the village Gājānūru in Uđuvańka-nāđu, lands in Haradanahaļji-sthaļa as also the village Puṇajūru, yielding an annual income of 44 gadyānas , by the gauđas of the village Hongaṇṇihaļli for worship and offerings and burning a perpetual lamp in the temple of god Divyaljīngēśvara Aṇilēśvara of Haradanahaļji in Eṇṇe-nāđu. It refers to the rule of Dēvarāya (II) of Vijayanagara and mentions Dēvadaṇṇāyaka.

cells.date: Śaka 1497, Viśvāvasu, Mārgaśira śu. 15, Monday=1545 A.D., November 18, Wednesday
cells.reference: EC., IV (Rev. 1975), Ch. 217; IV (I edn.), Ch. 77
cells.object: On a stone.
cells.remarks: Records a grant of a village (name lost) in Kundaghaṭta-sthala, of Nāgivalī-sthala and Hadināđu-sime, free all taxes, in the presence of god Gaṅgādhara of Śriraṅgapaṭtana, for feeding in a Viraśaiva-maṭha at Ummattūru. cells.object: On a slab set up in a field.
cells.remarks: Registers the grant of the village Kollagauṇđanapura, a hamlet ( kāluvaļi ) of the village Ummattūru, free of taxes like sumka and suvarṇādāya and with the right of forest cultivation ( kādāramba ), wet cultivation ( nirāramba ), tōṭa , tuđige etc. for services in the temple of god Bhujaṅgēśvara in Ummattūru. text.remarks: Records the grant of 30  gadyāṇas  by all the  mahājanas  of  agrahāra  Prasanna Vijayapura for maintaining dancing girls for the  pātrabhōga  service of god Rāmanātha of the village. States that Chikka Kampaṇṇa was ruling the kingdom. The amount was collected by each cultivator ( okkalu ) at fixed rate.

cells.date: Śaka 1437, Īśvara, Kārttika śu. 12, Utihāna-dvādaśi = 1517 A.D., October 26, Monday. But the Śaka year was 1439.
cells.reference: EC., III (Rev. 1974), Gu. 1; IV (I edn.), Gu. 30
cells.object: Copper-plate in the possession of Veńkaṭavaradāchārya, son of Śaurirāja-paṇdita.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of the village Mādalavāđi known as Kṛishṇasāgara, in Terakaṇāmbi-mahārājya, to Śrīnivāsa belonging to Kāśyapa-gōtra, Āpastambha-sūtra and Yajuś-śākha son of Gōpinātha, for offerings and worship of god Viṭṭhala, on the bank of the Tuṅgabhadrā. It gives a genealogical account of the king and enumerates the great gifts made by him, as is usually found in his copper-plate grants. The boundaries of the gift village are given in Kannada The record was written by Sabhāpati and engraved by Viraṇāchārya, son of Mallaṇa.

cells.date: Šaka 1518, Durmukhi, Vaiśākha ba. 12, Monday = 1656 A.D., May 12

cells.date: Šaka 142[7], Krōdhana, Phālguṇa śu. 4, Mina-saṁkrānti = 1506 A.D., February 27, Friday
cells.object: On a stone to the west of the village site.
cells.remarks: But the saṁkrānti fell on February 25, Wednesday. Slightly damaged. Records the gift of the village Honnakahaļļi in Kuđugu-nāđu of Terakaṇāmbe-nāđu, as an agrahāra renamed Chikkarāyapura and exempted from several taxes like kūṭade ṛe,eleya-tarugu, jiyara-te ṛige, mādā ṛike and uppina kāvali , to Raṅganātha-bhatṭa, son of Lakshmi-dikshita of Bhāradvāja-gōtra, Āpastambha-sūtra and Yajuś-śākhā. Also records the bestowment of the office of priesthood ( āchāryaka ) upon the donee while making a gift called mahābhūtaghaṭa in course of performing sixteen mahādānas , in the presence of god Raṅganātha, on the bank of Chandra-pushkaraṇi, situated between the two Kāvēris. Terakaṇāmbe-nāđu was being governed by Vira Chikkarāja-vođeya, son of Dēpaṇṇa-vođeya of solar race bearing the title Penugoṇđa-chakrēśvara etc.

cells.date: Šaka 1444, Vishu, Pushya ba. 30, Saturday, Makara-samkrānti, solar eclipse, Bhāskara-nakshatra = 1521 A.D., December 28, Pūrvāshāđha-nakshatra. There was no solar eclipse on the day. The Šaka year was current.
cells.object: On a stone near Mārishrīne.
cells.remarks: Registers a grant of money income derived from several professional taxes levied on the braziers, gaṇāchāras , vōjas , dāsu , āhaļa , washerman, barber, potter and those on oil-mill, salt, weaver's loom and others like mādārike and seṭiyūra-varttane , in the villages of Kōđihaļļi and its hamlets Aṇṇeyūru and Channayanapura situated in Terakaṇāmbi-sthaļa, by Sāļuva Gōvindarāja-vođeya, son of Gchirāja of Kauṇđinya-gōtra, Āśvalāyana-sūtra and Yajuś-śākhā who had received the territory for his nāyakatana by the king. The gift was made for the worship of and offerings to god Triyambakadēva on the eve of makara-samkrānti in the presence of god Virūpāksha, on the bank of the river Tuṅgabhadrā, for the welfare of the king.

cells.date: Šaka 1489, Kilaka, Šrāvaṇa śu. 10, Sunday. The details are irregular. However, the year Kilaka fell in Šaka 1470, when the details correspond to 1548 A.D., July 15, Sunday.
cells.object: On a stone to the east of the Gaṇapati temple.
cells.remarks: Records a grant of two villages, Kōṭeyakere in Terakaṇāmbi-sthaļa with its hamlet Rāma-napura and another (name lost) to Bōļa Nañjayadēva of Marihaļļi, on rental basis ( guttige ) by Sūrappa-ārichani, the agent of the king, with permission to enjoy the lands and other incomes from taxes like phaļadāya , manevaṇa , āđade xe etc. The nāyakatana of Terakaṇāmbī-sthaļa appears to have been bestowed upon the donor by the king. The lower portion of the record is worn out.

cells.reference: EC., III (Rev. 1974), Gu 121; IV (1 edn.), Gu. 10

cells.remarks: Registers a gift of the village Puttanapura in Hangaļa-sthaļa of Terakaṇāmbi-sime by Narasarājayya, the chief of Mysore who had received the sime from the king for his governance. cells.reference: EC., III (Rev. 1974), Gu. 61; XIV (1 edn.) Gu. 148
cells.remarks: Set of two copper-plates in the possession of the svāmi of Toṭṭihaṭīi. Engraved on two copper-plates of unequal size, this is said to have been issued during the reign-period of Harihara ruling from Śiraṅgapaṭṭaṇa and purports to register a grant of the village Sōmṇāthapura to his preceptor Śivaliṅgasvāmi of Rēṣuka-gōtra. Āpastambha-sūtra and Sāmajarishi-pravara, disciple (?) of Rēṣaṇārādhyasvāmi of Vijayanagara, by the king who also got built a maṭha for him at Sōsale. Thereafter it gives a list of his disciplines from several places. The record in a very faulty language, is full of orthographical errors.

cells.date: Śaka 1432, Hēmaṭambi, Jyēshṭha ba. 1, Mūlā-nākshatra. The Śaka year 1432 may be a mistake for 1339 corresponding to Hēmaṭambi. The other given details correspond to 1417 A.D., May 31, the constellation being Mūlā.
cells.reference: EC., III (Rev. 1974), Gu. 149; XIV (1 edn.), Gu. 128
cells.object: On a set of three copper-plates in the possession of the priest of the Triyaṭbakēśvara temple.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of money income lands and levies on betel palms to god Gurumūrti Triyambakadēva of Triyaṭbakapura in Terakaṇāmbe-sthaṭa. The pedigree of the king is given thus : Bukka II is not known to have had a son Harihara. But Dēvarāya I, brother of Bukka II, had a son Harihara. It is probably this Harihara that is mentioned here. A nephew to be mentioned as 'son' was not an uncommon practice then.

cells.date: Śaka 1369, Prabhava, Mārgaśira ba. 12, Friday=1448 A D. February 2.
cells.object: On a set of three copper-plates in the possession of the priest of Triyaṅbakēśvara temple.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of the village Kāṅasūru, renamed Prauṅhadēvarāyapura, along with its three hamlets, Beṭṭadabiṅu, Kailōṭi and Kētaha!li, situated in Kottaṅgāla-sthala of Arandavvālika-vēṅthe in the Hosapaṭṭaṇa-rājya of the Hoysala country, to a certain number of Brāhmaṇas on the occasion of performing the tulāpurusha-mahādāna . Nṛisimha, son of Dvēdi Kēsari-bhaṭṭa of Kāśyapa-gōtra, the composer of the inscription also received one vṛitti in the gift land, while Śrigiri Sakalāchārya, son of Varadāchārya, the śāsanāchā ya (record-keeper ?) also got 2 vṛittis . The record recounts the genealogy of the king and says that Mallikārjuna was so named as he was born by the favour of god Mallikārjuna of Śrigiri.

cells.date: Śaka 1435, Śrīmukha, Āśvija śu. 13=1513 A D., October 4
cells.reference: EC., III (Rev. 1974), Gu. 139; IV (I edn.), Gu. 3
cells.object: Stone set up inside the main entrance to the north of the Triyaṅbakēśvara temple.
cells.remarks: Records the gift of income from several taxes like beṭṭada-kāvalu , upiliga-kāvali sumka , siriyūra vartane etc., which were being remitted to the treasury at Terakaṇāmbi from Triyambakapnra, Maddūru and hamlets attached to it which had been donated to god Triyambakādeva free from all imposts ( sarvāmanya ), for the supply of camphor and betel-leaves for the god. Besides this, the income of other villages which belonged to the donor and of Mādhavapaṭṭaṇa purchased by him was also granted for the same god. The grant was made by Sāļuva Gōvindarājayya, son of Rāchirāja for the merit of the king. It is stated that the Terakaṇāmbi-sīme belonged to the chieftaincy of the donor.

cells.date: Šaka 1443, Vishu, Pushya śu. 3, Makara-saṁkrānti = 1521 A.D., December 2 on which day however, there was no  saṁkrānti .
cells.reference: EC., III (Rev. 1974), Gu. 150; XIV (I edn.), Gu. 129
cells.object: On a set of two copper-plates in the possession of the priest.
cells.remarks: Registers a grant of several villages, and income from taxes like those on gaṇas , potters, sheep, basketry, houses, uppina kāvali , excluding the hora-terige due from the temple villages, to god Triyambakēśvara of Triyambakapura by the king. It also specifies tax on looms, jaggery, sheep on barbers, oil mongers, vojas etc. The record gives details of gift villages some of which were actually purchased from the respective mahājanas . Sabhāpati is the composer of this record and the engraver Vīraṇāchārya, son of Mallaṇāchārya.

cells.remarks: Records a gift of income of 477 gadyṇṇas , from Kōdihalli in Terakaṇāmbe-sthaļa and its two hamlets-Aṇṇiyūru and Channayyanapura-besides income from several taxes like beṭṭada-kāvalu , āhaļadeḥe , hōgāḥadeḥe , gaṇākārateḥe , taxes on vōju , washeimen ( asaga ), barbers, potters, looms, mādṇḥe (basket weavers) etc. to god Triyambakadēva by Sāļuva Gōvindarāja, son of Rāchirāja. cells.date: Šaka 1457, Manmatha, Kārttika šu. 15=1535 A.D., November 9, Tuesday
cells.remarks: Basement stone of Triyambakēśvara temple. This is a sale deed registering the sale of sarvamānya lands in Hullāṇa alias Kāmalāpura-agrahāra in Pađuganāđa-sthaļa of Terakapāmbe-sime by Ayyappa, son of Nañjinātha-jöyisa of Vašishṭha-gōtra, Drāhyāyaṇa-sūtra and Sāma-śākha, the sthānika of the temple of Triyambakapura, to that god for a sum of 250 varahas , during the management ( pārupatya ) of Bhāskarayya, agent of Rāmābhaṭtayya. The amount was made over to the treasury of the temple. Witnesses are cited.

cells.date: 1. Šaka 1526, Višvāvasu, Vaišākha šu. 5
cells.object: Stone near a well to the north of the village.
cells.remarks: 2. Šaka 1576, Jaya, Vaišākha šu. 15, Friday=1654 A.D., April 21 The first part of the record states that on the first date Šānkarayya, agent for the affairs of the king Tirumalarājayya, son of Vīra Veñkaṭapatirāya had the well constructed for the use of the temple of god Triyambakēśvara. He is said to have got it released from the hands of (purchased from ?) Nāgāṇṇa-voḍeya who was a subordinate of mahāpradhāna Bayichaya-daṇḍanātha and is described as Hoyisaĵa-rājādhipati . The donor was a disciple of Paṇḍitadēva of Arundale-gaṇa, who appears to have been the preceptor also of Nāgaṇṇa-voḍeya.

cells.date: Śaka 1414 (expressed by the chronogram  bhāgya-bhāgye ) Paridhāvi, Phālguṇa ba. 7, Sunday, Mūlā = 1493 A.D., March 10
cells.remarks: Chākēnahaḥi (Dēmasamudra) copper-plate grant. It refers to the rule of Sāĵuva Narasimha, gives his genealogy and eulogises his achievements. States that Nāga-nāyaka, son of Malla-nāyaka and Tippāmbe represented to the king that under his order and the money provided by him, a tank had been excavated and forty Brāhmaṇas well-versed in different branches of learning had been brought and that an agrahāra needs to be settled on them. Thereupon, the king made a grant of the village Chākēnahaḥi, also called Dēmasamudra, situated in Maṇiyūra Honnayanahaḥi-sṭhaĵa, in Chōĵlasamudra-hōbaḥi of Makara-vēṇthe in Hiriya-chāvaḍi of Vidyānagara. Bhairavāchārya, son of Tippayāchārya engraved the record

cells.object: Stone set up near  jāpadakajte  of the deserted village Mođa!li.
cells.remarks: EC. IV (Rev. 1975), Ko. 62 This is a charter recording the establishment of a new settlement named Kamparājapaṭṭaṇa at Mođehaļļi by the orders of Kampaṇṇa-vođeya (Kamparāja), son of Bukkaṇṇa-vođeya, the Vijayanagara king. It lays down certain privileges and remits certain taxes like tappu , tavuđi , fines etc., for the inhabitants following different professions, binugu praje (artisans), including blacksmith, ( kammāra ), oil monger ( telligi ), barber ( nāvida ) and washerman in the two villages, viz. , Mōđihaļļi and Siṅganallūru, within the jurisdiction of Muđigoṇđa-Māmbaļļi, in Baṇđehaļi-rājya, by Hāle-šeṭṭi, at the instance of Kampaṇṇa-vođeya. It is said to be a charter presented to Rākaṇṇa, the paṭṭaṇasvāmi of Mōđihaļi, Siṅganallūru and other chiefs of the place. Some of the rights were : The artisans were exempted from paying tappu , taūđi , daṇđa , vuṇđige etc. The property of the elder would belong to the younger and of the younger to the elder (in case of death ?) and the daughter also had a share. Heirless property would go for the upkeep of tank and the temples. A thief, murderer etc. could be expelled. Banada Chauđēśvari (the goddess ?), the nādu , Sivanamķārā dēva (?) are cited as signatories.

cells.object: On a stone in front of the Basavēšvara temple.
cells.remarks: This refers to the rule of mahāmaṇđalēšvara Vira Achyutarāya. Rāmābhaṭtayya, the officer under the king, is said to have collected 30 varahas towards sambaļa-sarati from the village Kuntūru after some disorder ( telugānya ) had taken place thereat. This amount had been actually gifted to Nañjayyadēva of Sālūru, a Viraśaiva priest, as sarvamānya , But, while the officer was returning after collection, he met the priest who blessed him, whereupon, Rāmābhaṭtayya, in the presence of god Virūpāksha of Pampā-kshētra, for his merit, once again made that village free from taxes like sambaļa , sarati , kāṇike , beđige , varu and virāđa .

cells.date: Kali 4522, Šaka 1330, Sarvadhāri, Šrāvaṇa śu. 13. Va[đđavāra ?]=1408 A.D., August 4, Saturday. The Kali year was 4509 and not 4522.
cells.remarks: Another stone in the enclosure of the same temple. This refers to the rule of Vira Dēvarāya, son of Harihararāya. This is a charte. laying down the conditions and terms upon which the okkalu of handineṇtu-samaya were settled in the village Ha!i Hiriyūru. Some interesting conditions are : The farmers were to pay stipulated taxes to the palace and the fodder, grain, bullocks, ghee etc., due to the palace will be paid by turn by each family and they receive remission also in turns. Farmers by birth or domicile need not pay uṇđige . If the farmers fled, the hadineṇtu-samaya were to bring them back and pay the dues to the palace. Nāđa-sēnabōya Rāyappa wrote the record.

cells.date: Šaka 1498, Dhātu, Pushya śu. 13, Wednesday=1577 A.D., January 2
cells.object: Stone set up near the village entrance.
cells.remarks: EC. V (Rev. 1976), Kn. 104; IV (1 edn.), Yd. 59 Records the grant of a village Gaļigēkere in Hampāpura-sthala, renaming it as Rāmāpura, by Veňkatappa-nāyaka, son of Bavyappa-nāyaka's akīshṇappa-nāyaka (the chief of Bēlūru) to Vithala-bhaṭṭa, son of Rāmachandra-bahṭṭa of Kāśyapa-gōtra, and Āpastamba-sūtra as a sarvamānya-agrahāra , exempt from taxes like bālji, kūṭa, bēṭe, bēgāra-suňka , etc., for the merit of his mother Rāmamma, after whom the village was renamed. The donor is described as Maṇināgapuravarādhiśvara , Sindu-gövinda and Turākadala-vibāḍa .

cells.remarks: Records the grant of the village Hebasūru situated in Koṅganāḍu-vishaya, on the north bank of the Kāvēri, in Hoyisaṇa-dēśa with its ten hamlets, converting it into an agrahāra , renamed Bukkarāyapura, to various Brāhmaṇas of different gōtra and sūtras , by the king, for the merit of his father, who died on the date of the record. The hamlets named are 11 and not 10-Lōkupe, Gumanapalli, Gāyanapali, Saragūru, Horaveyapali, Aṭkaṇagaṭa, Haradanapali, Voṭarapali, Bidarahala, Mādaṇṇapali and Sanyapati.

cells.date: Šaka 1564, Chitabhānu, Phālguṇa ba. 3, Friday=1643 A.D., March 10
cells.object: On a stone in a grass land to the southeast of the village.
cells.remarks: Mārchahaļļi Registers a gift of the village Mārarchahaļļi, renamed Narasarājapura and the eight hamlets (Āyarahaļļi, Hāravahaļļi, Kālūru, Malvaļļi. cells.date: Šaka 1451, Manmatha, Kārttika šu. 12, Sthiravāra = 1535 A.D., November 6, Saturday.
cells.remarks: Set of 3 copper-plates purchased from Kṛishṇāchārya, now in the State Dept. of Archaeology. Registers a grant of the village Hiriyamaraļi altas Achyutāpura formed by combining two villages Bēvinakuppa and Chikkamaraļi in Kuruvaňka-nāđu of Šriraṅgapaṭṭaṇa-sime in Toṇđanūru-sthaļa of Hoyisaṇa-dēśa, to Kuppādhvari, son of Viśvēśādhvari of Kākalān-vaya, Apastambha-sūtra, Dēvarātasa-gōtra and Yajuś-śākha, a learned scholar, also described as Kavitā-chakravarti . cells.date: Šaka 1487, Krōdhana, Māgha šu. 12, Friday = 1566 A.D., February 1
cells.object: On a set of five copper-plates now in the office of the Director of Archaeology.
cells.remarks: Gives an account of the genealogies of the Tuļuva and Āraviđu families and records a gift of the village Yasyanū.u, with its hamlet, by the king to Sēshādryāchārya, son of Chittā-yārya of the Nallān Chakravarti family of Šrīvaishṇavas of Šrīvatsa-gōtra, at the request of his minister Tirumalarāya, brother of Rāmarāya, who made the request at the instance of Kṛishṇappa-nāyaka, son of Bayyappa-nāyaka, the chief of Bēlūru. The gift village, also called Kṛishṇāpura, was situated in Jayaṅgoṇḍaśōla-maṇḍala of Paḍavīdū-rājya and Paḍavūr-kōṭa, in Pirindimili-nādū Kalaveppaṭtu and Ventavāsi division. Rāmarāya is stated to have gone to the region of Vishṇu and his brother Tirumalarāya is described as karṇāṭa-rājya-śrī-sthāpanāchārya .

cells.king: Krishṇavarma-mahādhirāja (i.e. Krishṇarāya), son of Sāļuva Nārasimhavarma
cells.date: Śaka 1434, Śīmukha, Phālguṇa ba. 5. The cyclic year corresponds to Śaka 1435 when the given  tithi  occurred on 1514 A.D., March 15, Wednesday.
cells.object: On a stone near the village entrance.
cells.remarks: Records the gift of the village Kāvahalīli also called Kālihalīli, yielding a revenue of 130 gadyāṇas and 2 arahas , to god Kīrtinārāyaṇa of Talakāđu, by Sāļuva Timmarasa under the orders of the king, who is said to have come to the south on a conquering expedition. It further states that the processional image of the god and goddess. with ornaments, are sent from Vijayanagara, the capital. The grant was made at the request of Upavāsi-āchāri and for the merit of the king and Sāļuva Timmaya. The record professes to belong to the rule of Krīshṇavarma-mahārāja, son of Sāļuva Narasimhavarma. The king bears the titles associated with the Vijayanagara kings. But the introductory part of it is identical with a similar one found in the Gaṅga records.

cells.date: Śaka 1435 ( b riṇa-pāvaka-vēda-indu ) Śrimukha,  Rāmanavami  =1513 A.D., April 15. Tuesday
cells.object: On a set of 3 copper-plates in the same  maṭha .
cells.remarks: Refers to the reign-period of Rāmarāya, the chief of Āraviđu. Refers to his son, Śriraṅga-rāya by Lakkāmbike. Records the grant of six villages, in the presence of god Rāma Viṭhala at the time of the anointment of god Rāma, to Surēndra-yatindra, disciple of Raghunandana, himself a disciple of Jitāmitra-tirtha. The six villages granted were Ānehosūru, together with the maṭha at the Mayūra-kshētra in Mudugallu-dēśa, Lēpagiri in Koppaļa-dēśa, Sirugāpura in Gaṅgāvati-dēśa, Mallāpura and Honnamaṭte in Kushṭigi-dēśa and Hērakallu situated on the bank of the Tuṅgabhadrā in Źekkalakōṭa-dēśa. The engraver was Viraṇṇa's son Maṅgaṇāchārya.

cells.date: Śaka 1464 ( abdhi-aṅga-āmnāya-śitāmsu ) Śubhakrit, Māgha ba. 14, Śivarātri, Friday=1543 A.D. February 2
cells.object: On a set of copper-plates in the Rāghavēndrasvāmi-maṭha.
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of the village Komarakere situated in Kuṛugōđu-sime of Mūḍa-nāđu, belonging to Hastināvati, to Emmebasavēndra, a great devotee of Śiva, proficient in Viraśai-vāgama , by Tirumalarāya, son of Salakarāja, on the bank of the Tuṅgabhadrā, in the presence of god Virūpāksha The pedigree of the donor is given as : Lakkabhūpa m Tippamā Siṅgarāja m Chennāmbikā Salakarāja m Tippāmbika | Peda Timma Raṅga Raṅgarāya The record does not refer to any ruler, although the donor appears to have been ruling. The record is issued some months after the death of Achyutarāya when there was a dispute for succession between Veñkaṭādri, son of the deceased king and Sadāśiva whose cause was championed by Aļiya Rāmarāya. Salaka Tirumala, the maternal uncle of Veñkaṭādri upheld the cause of his nephew, and probably himself issued this grant, unless it is to be considered as spurious.

cells.date: Śaka 1497 ( aśva-ratna-payōdhi-indu ) Yuva, Āshāḍha śu 12=1575 A D., June 19, Sunday
cells.object: On three copper-plates in the same  maṭha .
cells.remarks: Registers a royal grant of the village Pudukkuḍi, containing 50 vṛittis and also the village Nāvalūru renamed Rāmachandrapura, situated in Nityavinōda śri-vaṭanāḍu of Tañjāvūru-sime in Chōla-maṇḍala to the pontiff Surēndra-tirtha, at the instance of Chavva-bhūpāla. The donee retained for himself 7 vṛittis for the worship of god Rāmachandra and distributed the remaining among several Brāhmaṇas. The record was written by Kavi-śāsana-svayaṁbhū, son of Sabhāpati and engraved by Gaṇapāchārya, son of Viraṇa. It gives the pedigree of the king.

cells.date: Virōdhi, Māgha ba. 2. Probably=1530 A.D., January 2, Saturday
cells.object: On a stone to the left of the  mukhamaṇṭapa  of the Sōmēšvara temple.
cells.remarks: This records an agreement between Bhadrayya, agent of mahā'naṇdalēśvara Ramarāja Tirumālarājayyadēva-mahā-arasu and the elders ( hlriyaru ) of the maṭha at Suttūru to the effect that the land in the village Holeya Suttūru of Tāyūru-sthala in Mūgūru-sime, originally granted to god Sōmēśvara of Suttūru was to be given to the maṭha and the annual rental of 40 varahas was to be paid to the temple treasury. The rental called śrōtriyada-gultige and the agreement śrōtriyada-kallupaṭṭe , were to come into effect for one year from Āsaāḍha śu. of the year Vikṭa to Jyēshṭha ba. 30 of Khara.

cells.date: Šaka 1529, Plavanga, Vaišākha šu 3=1607 A.D., April 19
cells.reference: EC., IV (Rev. 1975), PP. 59; IV (I edn.), Hs. 63
cells.object: On a stone in the backyard of a house.
cells.remarks: This is a stone charter issued by mahāmaṇdalēšvara Tirumalarājayadēva-mahā-arasu to the Chaṅgā|va chief Rudragaṇa, stating that he granted Maļalavāđi-sime for offerings etc. to god Annadāni Mallikārjuna so that merit accrue to his parents Rāmarājaya and Tim-mājamma. It also remitted the tribute ( pagudi ) due from Rudragaṇa alias Piriyarāja, son of Šrikanṭharāja, who was the son of Nañjuṇđarāja, The god Šelvapi|lai of Mēlukōṭe and the aļvārs are cited as witnesses to the grant. It states that Maļavāđi sime within the Nañjārāyapaṭṭaṇa-rājya is included in the puravarga of god Mallikārjuna and Rudragaṇa with the first name Piriyarāja is the ruler of Nañjārāyapaṭṭaṇa-rājya.

cells.date: Śaka 1463, Šārvari, Māgha ba. 14 = 1541 A.D., January 24, Tuesday. The Śaka year was current
cells.object: Stone in the Girijākalyāṇa-maṇṭapa in the enclosure of Hanumantēśvara temple.
cells.remarks: EC. V (Rev. 1976), TN. 55; III (I edn.), TN. 120 Records the grant of land (below the Kāvēri) and 900 arecanut trees, by Tamma-nāyaka, son of Kannapa-nāyaka who was himself the agent of Varadappaṇna, minister of the king, for conducting the car festival of god Hanumantēśvara of Vahnipura. It is said that the donor got a new chariot made to the god and consecrated the images of deities like Umāskandhēśvara and Vighnēśvara. The donor's wife Tippamma added some more lands for offering curd-rice ( dadyōdana ) to the god. The gift were made in the presence of the heb-bāras , gauḍus , mahājanas and the sēnabōva of the village Bannūru. The entire gift consisted of 7 khaṇḍugas of wet land and 900 areca trees. A supplement adds that the donor also made a gift of the tank to the west of Eḍeh 11i and lands situated below it.

cells.reference: EC., V (Rev. 1976), TN. 109; XIV (I edn.) TN. 165

cells.date: Šaka 1404, Kali year 3079, Šubhakřit, Chaitra šu. 5, Sunday=1482 A.D., March 24. The Kali year was 4583.
cells.reference: EC., V (Rev. 1975) TN. 237; XIV (1 edn.), TN. 222
cells.remarks: Pavement stone to the right, in front of the Janārdana temple. Sāyamma, mother of mahāmaṇdalēšvara Vira Sōmaṇṇa-nāyaka who was administering Hoysaļa-dēša, made a permanent exemption of 15 varahas to be paid to the royal treasury towards tax etc., on the land belonging to god Janārdana of Šrīraṅgapura alias Mālaṅgi, in Hadināđa-vēņthe, to the south of Kāvēri, for the worship of god and conducting festivals. The land appears to have been her personal fief ( mai-bhōga ). The record states that 3079 were the years of the Kali era of 43200 (years ?).

cells.king: Harihara II, son of Bukkarāya I
cells.date: Śaka 1319, Īśvara, Śravaṇa śu. 5, Sunday, Siṅha-saṅkrānti = 1397 A.D., July 29
cells.reference: EC., V (Rev. 1976), TN. 17; III (1 edn.), TN. 64
cells.object: On a set of 3 copper-plates in the Taluk treasury.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of the village Koļatūru in Channapaṭṭaṇa-baļila as ap agrahāra renamed Pratāpa Hariharapura, dividing it into 36 vṛittis gifted to 39 Brāhmaṇas. 32 of them got 1 vṛitti each, 5 of them got 1/2 vṛitti each and the remaining two 3/4 of a vṛitti each. The gift was made by Nārayanadēva-ođeya, nephew of the king and younger brother of mahāmaṇdalēśvara Mallappođeya (Mallinātha), in the presence of god Agastyanātha, on the confluence of the Kāvēri and the Kapilā, for the merit of his father i.e. , uncle, Pratāpa Harihara-mahārāya. The record describes itself as the śāsana of Koļatūru alias Pratāpa Hariharapura.

cells.date: Śaka 1544, Dundubhi, Phālguṇa śu. 15, Minōttara=1622 A D., March 16
cells.object: On a set of 5 copper-plates in the possession of a villager.
cells.remarks: EC . V (Rev. 1976), TN. 15; III (I edn.). TN. 62 Records the grant of two villages Navilūru and Āladūru in Tayūra-nāḍu, Mūgūra-sthala and Ummattūru-chāvaḍi, both of them being combined into an agrahāra of 33 vṛittis and named Chāmarāja-samudra, divided among as many Brāhmaṇas of variour gōtras and sūtras . One vṛitti was gifted to god Guñjā Narasimha, for the merit of Narasarājoḍeya. The grant was made by Chāmarājoḍeya, son of Narasarāja-vōḍeya and grandson of Rājoḍeya. It is said that before making such a grant, the king looked into an earlier copper-plate grant issued by Rājoḍeya with the permission of Veṅkaṭapatidēva-mahārāya who bestowed on Rājoḍeya, Ummattūru and Śirraṅgapaṭṭaṇa as kāṇḍḍchi . The date of this earlier charter was Śaka 1534, Paridhāvi, Chaitra śu. 5, i.e. , 1612 A.D., March 27.

cells.reference: EC., IV (Rev. 1975), YI. 168; XIV (1 edn.), YI. 190
cells.object: Inscribed slab buried near the well in the backyard of Liñgadaguđi
cells.remarks: Ālakere Registers a grant of land to a number of mahājanas (named) of Ālakeṛe and Benakeṛe, free from several taxes, for the merit of his master, by Sālūva Gōvindarājayya, the chief minister. The names of donees are given in Sanskrit.

cells.date: Šaka 1486, Raktākshi, Kārttika šu. 10=1564 A.D., October 15, Sunday
cells.reference: EC., IV (Rev. 1975), YI. 179; IV (I edn.), YI. 29
cells.object: On the backside of a stone in the backyard of a house.
cells.remarks: Registers the grant of four (?) villages, Gaṇiganūru, Basavaṇṇavođeyarapura, Tūbigeře and Sēnaguṇđila in Gaṇiganūru-sthaļa of Hadināđu-sīme, belonging to the chieftaincy of Jagadēkarāya-vođeya, as rakta-kođage , to Chāmarasa-vođeya by Divāṇada-vođeya, as a compensation since the donee's father Dēvappa-gauđa was killed unjustly by Sañjarakhān. The record states that six villages were granted; but only four are named. Divāṇada-vođeya may be interpreted as the vođeya (chief) of the divāṇa i.e., district, of the sīme whose name is not clear.

cells.date: Kali 4470, Saumya, Šrāvaṇa. The Šaka year is lost. The details correspond to 1359 A.D. July-August.
cells.object: On a stone lying behind the Vaid, ēšvara temple.
cells.remarks: This refers to the rule of mahāmaṇđalēšvara Kumāra Kampaṇṇa-vođeya and registers four separate gifts; (i) cocoanut garden and 15 houses to god Vaidyanātha of Māmba||i described as Hariharanātha-paṭṭaṇa by Appa-nāyaka; (ii) cocoanut garden in front of Sāma-kadēvi by Dēvaṇṇa-seṭti, son of Māri-seṭti, after purchase from Kāli setti, son of Āṇđāru-seṭti, for the worship and offerings and a perpetual lamp to god Tīvaga-nāyanār, consecrated by him; (iii) cocoanut and jack-tree gardens, as purāṇa-vṛitti and for offreings and lamp to god Vaijanāthadēva by Seṭtiyaṇṇa and (iv) two dēvadāna gardens to the same deity by Āṇđāru-seṭti.

cells.date: Śaka 1304 ( chandra-anala-nabha-vēda ), Rudhirōdgāri= 1383-84 A.D. The Śaka year would be 1305.
cells.remarks: AR1E., 1958-59, No. 682 Boulder on the bank of the river near the ferry. States that Kampa-ĵLūpa, son of Harihara ( Harihara-ātmaja ), had a path made to the Tuṅgabhadrā. We know that Kampaṇa or Kumāra Kampa was the younger brother of Harihara II, during whose reign our record was inscribed. The expression Harihar-ātmaja in our record may therefore be a mistake for Harihar-ānuja . In that case, this is the latest known date for Kampa, although it is not impossible that Harihara II had also a son named Kampa.

cells.date: Śaka 1358, Nala, Mārgaśira śu. 15, Friday =1436 A.D., November 23
cells.object: Stone in  the sculptured  maṇḍapa  inside the fort.
cells.remarks: Rāhuttarāya Viraṇṇa, son of simpiga Bhūtanātha of Mūḍugallu having raided the hill fort ( beṭṭada-kōṭe ) of the Sultān ( suritāna ) brought the golden pinnacle as a trophy which pleased the king to whom it was sent. At the king's instance the hero was honoured by granting him the privilege of mēṭigoļaga in several villages including Mudugallu by Varadaṇṇa-nāyaka who was holding the Mudugallu-nāđu as nāyakatana under the king. Tippōja the stone mason, was also rewarded with meṭigoļaga at Hiriya Eṛadahaļi. The privilege seems to be one of collecting grains from the agriculturists at the time of harvest. The record shows that this region was under Vijayanagara on the date and perhaps even for some more time. Cf. Sewell and Aiyangar HISI , p. 2.6.

States that the king, after his conquest of Rāchūru, Alampūru, Mānave, Hānuṅgalu and Māgađe forts, visited Kūđalūru at the confluence of the Krīshṇā and Bhimarathī and made a grant of the village Chikalaparavi in Mānuve-sīme to god Tiruveṅgalanātha while performing the  ratna-dhēnu ,  gōsahasra  and  kanakāśva mahādānas  in association with his queens Chinnādēvi and Tirumaladēvi. Contains a long  praśasti  of the king.

cells.date: Śaka 1473, Virōdhikīit, Āshāḥha, śu. 12, Monday=1551 A.D., June 15
cells.reference: ARSIE., 1914-15, No. A 1; EI., XIV, No. 16
cells.object: On the copper-plates received from the Collector of Raichur.
cells.remarks: Raichur Gives the geneology of Rāmarāja and records the grant of the village Bēvinahallī, surnamed Rāmasamudram, with a small hamlet Ponnāpuri as gaṇa-bhōgyam and sarvamānya to learned Brāhmaṇas of various gōtras and sūtras , made by Rāmarāja the Karṇāṭa minister and brother-in-law of the king. The grant was made at the request of a subordinate Muhammadan chieftain Ainana Malukka, who seems to have been a great patron of Brāhmaṇas. The village granted is divided into 135 vrittis and 133-2/3 vrittis are allotted to various Brāhmaṇas and ministers of the king, and the remaining vrittis to gods.
