cells.date: Šaka 1301, Siddhārthi, Jyēshṭha-pūrṇimā, Tuesday=1379 A.D., May 31
cells.remarks: Kuknūr Copy of a copper-plate in the possession of Dēsāyi family. (original not traced). The copy is in Kannada although it is said that the original is in Nāgari. Registers the whole-ale grant of the entire village Kukanūru by the king at the instance of the royal preceptor Kriyāśakti bearing the titles Rājaguru , mahāmaṇdalāchārya and vaṇivilāsa to Gaṇḍ na Bhaṭṭappayya, the high priest of the religious establishment of the goddess Mahāmāyā and the chief of the one thousand mahājanas of the primeval agrahāra of Kukanūr. The grant was made to wicld full authority over the township and take suitable steps for the rehabilitation of the ruined agrahāra of Kukanūr, as also to renovate the temple of Mahāmāyā and other shrines, arrange for the worship, offerings and burning of lamps etc. and for establishing seminaries for the study of the vēdas.

cells.remarks: KanlaJa Śaka 1483, Durmati, Pushya śu. 10 = 1561 A.D., December 16, Tuesday States that the gateway of the temple having collapsed on account of breakage during the disturbances of the Turakas who set fire to the capital ( Turaka rājyadhāni suṭu kaṭunaṭ. naḍadu bāgilu muḍidu bīḍu iralāgi ) Dēvarāya-gauḍa, dēsāyi of Kukanūru-sime got it re-constructed. cells.date: Śaka 1485, Dundubbi, Āshāḥha śu. 3, Śukravāra = 1562 A.D., June 5. The Śaka year was current.
cells.object: On a stone in the Siriyappana  guđi  behind the Īśvara temple.
cells.remarks: Dilāvara-vođeya, the ṭhāṇādār of Dummi-sime, which had been bestowed upon Maluka-vođeya as amara , having harassed the gauđa-praje and nāyakas of the area, Pillappa-nāyaka, son of Hanume-nāyaka of Santhebennūru and Gauđayya of Chikkagañgūru in Dummi-sthala were proceeding to meet and report to Maluka-vođeya when they were attacked on the way and Gauđayya was killed. Maluka-vođeya having heard this, sent his ūlīga Chimana-vođeya and through him made a grant of land in Chikkagañgūru to the descendants of Gauḍayya as nettam-goḍage , and bestowed Dummi-sime upon Pilla-nāyaka. Dilāvar, the thāṇādār was suitably punished.

cells.remarks: A number of gauḍas and others made a grant of the village Auvkananagōṇte in Ānavēri-nāḍ, for the perpetual lamp and offerings to god Rāmēśvara of Kuruva. cells.date: Šaka 1129, Sarvajit, Māgha šu. 10, Sunday. Irregular. The Šaka year appears to be a mistake for 1329, when the  tithi  occurred on 1408 A.D., January 8.
cells.object: Hero-stone set up to the east of a garden.
cells.remarks: Haritālū Viraṇṇaođeya, son of Bommaṇṇa-ođeya and grandson of Ráyapa-ođeya was administering the 18 kampanas of Āraga, when Bōlaya Bommeya-nāyaka, the Bēđa chief having raided created havoc in the region. At the instance of the king, Viraṇṇa-vođeya and other gauđas named including the mahāprabhu of Haratālū, fell on the bēđas 3 and 6 drove them away, killing several, justifying thereby the title mūvara-rāyara-gayđa bestowed upon them (their ancestors ?) by Harihara-mahārāya and mahāpradhāna Guṇđappa-daṇṇāyaka. In the battle Tirika-gauđa died and his wife Bommayakka committed sahagamana .

cells.date: Śaka 1290, Plavanga. Kārttika śu. 1, Monday=1367 A.D., October 24, Sunday, f.d.t. .02
cells.object: Stone before the Ēśvara temple.
cells.remarks: Damaged. When Vira Bukkaraya's son Vira Viruparaya, and his pradhāna (minister) Taļa-kāđa Māvarasa were ruling the Āraga-18 kampaṇas and the Gutti-18 kampaṇas with Iđu-guṇđi and Konkaṇa and Hoysaṇa kingdoms as the boundary, a gift was made of the village Gaṇali for worship and offerings to god Śaṅkara of Kō[đūru ?] in Aivattu-nāđu for the prosperity and good of Viruparāya, probably by the minister. The gift appears to have been made over to Hariyaṇṇa-sēnabōva and Machaya-nāyaka who were to maintain the same. Mādója appears to be the sculptor.

cells.date: Šaka 1474, Virōdhikřitu, Māgha ba. 30, Wednesday = 1552 A.D., February 24. The Šaka year was current.
cells.remarks: The stone set up in the verandah of the małha of the same village. When Sadāśivarāya-nāyaka of Keładi was ruling the eighteen kampańas of Āraga and Bańkiyarasa Šāńkaradēvi-amma the Honneyakambałi-vođeya was ruling the Muńgi-nāđu, Kabu-nāđu and Hosa-nāđu of Āraga-sime which they had received for hereditary chieftaincy ( kāṇachi ) from the Keładi chief, a charter was issued declaring that the property of all those who died without heir would be distributed among the descendants of the same gōtra , and if no such descendant was available it would be made over to the temple and that in no case it would be seized by the king as aputrika-sādaṇđa . The record was written by Lingaṇa-sēnabōva and ergraved by Gaurayya, the stone mason, described as chitrika .

cells.date: Šaka 1488. Kshaya, Šrāvaṇa šu. 13, Monday = 1566 A.D., July 29
cells.remarks: Forth stone in the same place. This registers a grant of land in Madavali by Kēšappa-adhikāri, son of Gövinda-adhikāri of Hebbalage in Nilamaneya-apayika, after purchase from the gauđas and Lińgappa, the nāđa-sēnabōva of that village, to god Šambhulińga of Uđukunđa, for the daily feeding of 8 Brāhmanas. Immađi Sadāśivarā, a-nāyaka was ruling Āraga-rājya as māgaṇi and at his pleasure Bańkiyarasa Honneya-kambałi-ođeya, Ammidēvi-amma was administering the region above the ghats. The land was purchased by the donor as brahmasva , free from all taxes.

cells.date: Śaka 1488, Kshaya, Āśvija śu. 2, Sunday = 1566 A D., September 15
cells.remarks: First stone in the verandah of Šambhuliūga temple. When Immadi Sadāśivarāya-nāyaka was ruling Āraga-rājya as his māgaṇe and Bañkiyarasa Honneyakambali-ođeya and Ammidēvi amma were governing Muñgi-nāđu, Kabbu-nāđu and other countries above the ghats, Kēśappa-adhikāri son of Gövinda-adhikāri of Vaśishṭha-gōtra, belonging to Hebbalage of Nelamaneya-payika, made a gift of land yielding a fixed income ( siddāya ) of 80 khaṇđugas in Būvanakoppa of Kabbunāđa-sīme, to god Šambhuliūga of Uđukunda to the west of Kabbu-nāđu, in the nine kampaṇas of Āraga-vēṇte. The king is said to belong to Harihararāya-vamśa.

cells.date: Śaka 1488, Kshaya, Āśvija śu. 2, Sunday=1566 A.D., September 15
cells.remarks: Third stone in the verandah of the same temple. Immađi Sadāśivarāya-nāyaka was governing Āraga-rājya. Records a grant of land situated in the village Taguđari in Kabbu-nāđu-sīme yielding an income of 100 khaṇđugas of paddy and 14 haṇas of siddāya by Bańkiyarasa Honneyakambaļi-ođeya and Ammidēvi-amma to god Šambhuliūga of the temple built by Kēšappa-adhikāri of Bidirūru, at Uđukunda situated to the west of Kabbu-nāđu, one of the nine kampaṇas of Āraga-vēnthe. The siddāya was derived from the tax on forest kāna-texu amounting to 1 ga and 4 ( haṇa ?), i.e. 14 haṇas . It was stipulated that besides offerings to the deity and burning lamps, 2 Brāhmaṇas were also to be fed daily in the feeding house ( chatra ). The king is said to belong to the family of Harihara.āya.

cells.object: Stone set up in the enclosure of Srinivasa Rao's Rice Mill.
cells.remarks: The top portion of the record is lost. It refers to a Lakshmaṇa-sēnabōva of Kabbu-nāđu. After the imprecatory verses another record is engraved. Sadāśivarāya-nāyaka is stated to be governing Yichchhe-9 kampaṇa in Āraga-vēṇthe as māgaṇi at the instance of the king ; and under his instructions Bañkiyarasa Honneya Kambaļi-vođeya and Śañkaradēvi-amma were governing Bidirū.u in Muñgi-nāđu, Kabbu-nāđu etc., above the ghats. It registers a grant of some land yielding one varaha to the Nirāsi-maṭha of Jāligekanteya Kalyāṇa-vođeya of Dēvara Bidirūru. It is stated that the gift land had been originally given to the donor's predecessors as nettarugođage . Liñgaṇṇa, son of Lakshmaṇa-sēnabōva of Kabbu-nāđu, wrote the record.

cells.object: On a more set of 3 copper-plates.
cells.remarks: Records the gift of 10 villages (named) situated in Honnekoppa in Ara-nāđu as sarvamānya for the am:itapađi of god Rāmachandra made over to the pontiff Rāghavēśvara-bhāratisvāmi described as Śriṅgapuravarādhīśvara by Sōmaṇa-nāyaka. The gift was made in the presence of god Virūpāksha, on the bank of the Tuṅgabhadrā. This seems to be a confirmation of an earlier grant made in the year Dundubhi, Pushya, solar eclipse, in Śūrpālaya-kshētra on the bank of the Kṛishṇavēṇi. The donor is described as rājadhirāja paramēśvara , mūru-rayara-gaṇḍa . The record composed by Viraṇa was engraved by Aṇṇāchārya.

cells.date: Śaka 1321 (expired), 1322 (current), Pramāthi, Kārttika śu. 15, Wednesday, lunar eclipse=1399 A.D. October 15, (Adhika Kārttika)
cells.remarks: Gauja-agrahāra A set of 3 copper-plates in the possession of patēl Rāmappa. Bāchaṇṇa-vođeya, described as mahāmantriśvara , ruling Koñkaṇa-rājya and Chandragutti-rājya from Gōva-nagara, made a gift of the village Kaṇavapura in Hoṇahađe-nāđu in Chadragutti-vēṇṭheya to certain Brāhmaṇas as niyataśītōtra , free from taxes. It was made into an agrahāra of 27 vrittis yielding an annual revenue of 276 hons and 5 haṇas from the month of Kārttika. The taxes listed viz., uppinakāyakambi (tax on jars of pickles ?), nāđa-sarathi , marana-biṭṭi (taxing of trees by force ?) and grāsa (feeding of king's servants ?) may be noted. Bāchaṇṇa, also called Bhāskara, is said to have succeeded Narahari and earlier to him Mādhava. Narahari was Bāchaṇṇa's elder brother.

cells.date: 1. Śaka 1395, Nandana, Vaiśākha śu. 13 = 1472 A.D., April 21, Tuesday, the Śaka year being current; 2. Śaka 1396, Vijaya, Kārttika śu. 5, Wednesday=1473 A.D., October 26, Tuesday, the Śaka year being current.
cells.object: On a stone in the Pārśvanātha-basti.
cells.remarks: The first part of the record states that when mahāprabhu Bhairaṇṇa-nāyaka, son of Munduvaṇṇa-nāyaka was governing Horaguppa Hebbayala-nāđu, Haivaṇṇa-nāyaka, Baliya-gauđa of Iđuvaṇi (the foremost of Ānevalige in Nagira-ṭhāvu)and Pārisa-gauđa, nephew of Bukkaṇṇa-nāyaka and son of Mālakka-nāyakiti, got built a chaityālaya at Yiđuvaṇi and consecrated Pārśva-tīrthēśvara therein. Bhairaṇṇa-nāyaka mentioned above, described as the lord of Aiśvaryapura and eulogised as Maleyahuliya-mārthaṇđa and Iđigay-eṇṭu-daṇđ-igeya manneyara gaṇđa , son of Siru-mādēvi, made a grant of land yielding a revenue of 2 ga 2 pa (22 paṇas ) for several services like Mrityuñjāyachakra-pūje , Siddhachakra-puje , anointment in milk etc. to god Pārśva-tīrthēśvara. On the second date, Bhairaṇṇa-nāyaka at the instance cf Vādīndra Viśálakīrti-bhaṭṭāraka, made a gift of land in Honnagōđu of Horaguppe Hebbayala-nāđu for worship and offerings of Nēmināthasvāmi of Malayakhēđa. The record was written by Yimmađi Bhairavēndra, son of Bhairaṇṇa-nāyaka.

cells.date: Śaka 1437, Vaiśākha śu. 3=1515 A.D., April 17, Tuesday, the cyclic year being Yuva.
cells.object: On a stone in front of Dūdihalĵi Channapa's house.
cells.remarks: Arasanagere EC. VII, Sk. 25 Triyambakarasa, son of Tipparasa, of Sivanasamudra who was himself the son of Haṇṇi Mādarasa of Vaśisṭha-gōtra and Āśvalāyana-sūtra, made a grant of the village Bairāpura, a hamlet (?) of Mādaravalĵi in Mālēnahalĵi-sime, which he had received for his chieftaincy by the king to Hariharārādhya, son of Mādhavārādhya of Hārita-gōtra, Āpastambha-sūtra belonging to Kōṭhiśānvaya, as an agrahara renamed Hariharapura. Since the land in the village was found to be insufficient for residential purposes, situated as it was on the bank of a rivulet, some more lands in Arisinagēri-sime was added to it. Triyambaka wrote the record. The gift was made on the occasion of a solar eclipse. But, no eclipse occurred in this, the previous or the next year, in the month cited.

VII, Sk. 25 Triyambakarasa, son of Tipparasa, of Sivanasamudra who was himself the son of Haṇṇi Mādarasa of Vaśisṭha-gōtra and Āśvalāyana-sūtra, made a grant of the village Bairāpura, a hamlet (?) of Mādaravalĵi in Mālēnahalĵi-sime, which he had received for his chieftaincy by the king to Hariharārādhya, son of Mādhavārādhya of Hārita-gōtra, Āpastambha-sūtra belonging to Kōṭhiśānvaya, as an  agrahara  renamed Hariharapura. Since the land in the village was found to be insufficient for residential purposes, situated as it was on the bank of a rivulet, some more lands in Arisinagēri-sime was added to it. Triyambaka wrote the record. The gift was made on the occasion of a solar eclipse. But, no eclipse occurred in this, the previous or the next year, in the month cited.

cells.date: Saka 1335, Sādhāraṇa, Kārttika ba. 13.  Tithi =1430 A.D., November 13, Monday, f J.t. .07 the Saka year being 1352.
cells.object: On a hero-stone built into the roof of the Virabhadra temple.
cells.remarks: When Handiyarāya, son of Arasappa, of the treasury ( bhaṇdārada ), was ruling Gove-Chandragutti-rājya. Sōvarasa attacked Posagunda, perhaps with the connivance of the sthānika of the Sōmayidēva temple of that place. In the fight Keñche-gauđa, son of Sāla-gauđa of Hannakere died. A gifi of land was made to his guru Šivarātraiyya-ođeya, for his merit by Nāga-gauđa, Kāmi-gauđa and Nāgarasi. Kalikōja, son of Tammōja engraved the stone.

cells.date: Šaka 1290 ( kha, randhra, kara, kumudabāndhava ) Kilaka, Šarat Kārttika,  Kīsh-āshṭan i  = 1368 A.D., November 3, Friday
cells.object: On a stone before the Kallēšvara temple.
cells.remarks: Mādhavāmātya, under orders of the king, was governing the western part of the kingdom. At the instance of Kāśivilāsa Kriyāśakti, the minister made a grant of the village Muchchanđi, renamed Vidyēšvarapura, situated in Nāgarakhaṇđa, in the 18 maṇđalas with Chandrakūṭapura as the chief maṇđala , within his own dominion for the worship and offerings of god Triyambakanātha. He also invited Brāhmaṇas of Kāśmira ( Kāśmira-brāhmaṇān ) well-versed in Śivāmnāya to settle down in the village which was for that purpose divided into 80 vrittis . The names of the donees are listed.

cells.date: Kali 4515, Śaka 1 . . , Mārgaśira, śu. 5, Thursday. In the Kali year 4516 corresponding to Kali 1337 the  tithi  occurred on 1415 A.D., November 7.
cells.object: On a stone to the south in the enclosure of the Lakshminarasimha temple.
cells.remarks: Mahānāyakāchārya Yeṛa Lakhe-nāyaka who was ruling Dummi-nāḍu and Bāṇura-nāḍu (?) having cleared away the forest, constructed a tank and built two villages Narasimhapura and Lakshmipura presented them to god Lakshminarasimha of Beñkiyapura (?). He remitted taxes on marriages, oil-cakes, customs on loads on cows, she-buffaloes, he-buffaloes, horses, carts, bullocks, etc. on the produce of the gardens belonging to these villages, the store houses, sugarcane mills, the transit dues on loads of betel leaf imported, transit dues in Beñkiyapura, on the areca of the rent-free garden attached to the temple in Bārandūru, by the order of the king, for the residents of these two villages. Siddapanṇa granted to the god the transit dues of the Bampkiyāpura-ṭhāṇa, and the transit dues let out on contract for articles coming from beyond the river. Harihara, mentioned herein, may be prince Harihara III.

cells.king: Pratāpa Dēvarāya, son of Vijayarāya ruling from Vijayanagara
cells.date: Śaka 1352, Sādhāraṇa, Pushya ba. 30, Sunday=1431 A.D., January 14
cells.remarks: Another stone in the same place. When Rāyaṇṇa-rāja (vođeya), son of Baichappa-daṇṇanāyaka, was ruling Āraga-rājya and Ānavēri-nāđu, Hoļeyahonnūru-nāđu and a part of Hanagavāđi-nāđu, all the gauđa-prajes of Hoļeyahonnūra-nāđu agreeing among themselves made him a gift of the village Daṇṇāyakapura for the chhatra and other works of merit which he established to please the gods Māhēśvara and Lakshminārāyaṇa in the presence of all the gods of Kūđali. The fixed revenue of the gift village, free of all taxes, is 155 honnu according to former rulers ( hiriya-maneyavaru ). They gave with this, 35 honnu which the nāyakavāđis formerly received including all garden etc and all taxes. This Daṇṇāyakapura was formed into a śrōtriya of 20 vriṭṭis and divided among Brāhmaṇas of Kūđali. They gave 8 honnu for the purpose of constructing a tank and planting gardens. The income from that Daṇṇāyakapura insufficient for the rest, they also gave 7 varahas from the customs-dues of Beļugali, belonging to god Narasimha. The 20 vritti holders like Chaṇđi-dikshita of Kūđali were to receive the gadyāṇas and maintain the charities at the feeding house and the temple.

cells.date: Śaka 1268, Vyaya, Māgha ba. 30, Sunday, Śatabhishā-akshatra, Siddhayōga, Nāga-karaṇa sun in Kumbha, solar eclipse=1347 A.D., February 11
cells.object: Copper-plate in the possession of Mallārappa, the  patēl .
cells.remarks: Contains, after some fine verses on Ganēśa, Śiva and Varāha, the praise of Samgama and his sons Harihara, Samgama, Bukka and Mārappa and Hastināgiri, capital of Harihara. Mārappa is described as governing the western kingdom with Chandragutti of Gōmanta-śaila as capital. His conquest upon the Kadamba king and the visit to Gōkarṇa the sacred place on the west coast are next described. The village Heddase, renamed Samgamapura was given away by him to Brāhmaṇas well-versed in vēdas and sāstras who had migrated from Āndhradēśa. His minister Mādhava, disciple of Kriyāśakti and author of a work consisting of the essence of Śaivāgama ( Tātparyadipika ) is next described. By his orders his subordinate named Bollurāja is stated to have got the present charter issued in consultation with the mahājanas of Elase and Kuppagadđe in Banavāsi province of Kuntala-dēśa. Boundaries of the village are specified.

cells.date: Šaka 1298, Nala, Āšvija šu. 12, Thursday =1376 A.D., September 25
cells.remarks: Sixth stone. Bechi-gauđa, disciple of Rāmachandra-maladhāridēva, son of Chanda-gauđa the mahā-prabhu of Āvali, died by pañchanamaskāra-vidhi . His youngest wife Muddi-gauṇđi committed sahagamana . Mādoja-Nāgoja, son of Gorabōja who (belonged to) the house-hold of Bechi-gauđa son of Chanda-gauđa who himself was the son of Masaṇa-gauđa who was the prabhu of Āvali, carved this stone. Gorava-gauḍa, Kāla-gauḍa and Gōpa-gauḍa were the other sons of Masaṇa-gauḍa.

cells.remarks: Third stone Sivamoga Distrifet Bhāva , Phālguṇa ba. 11, Wednesday =1395 A.D.. March 17; the Śaka year was 1317. In the time of the minister Hariparāya, Kāmi-gāuṇdi, wife of Kāna Rāmaṇa (?) and disciple of Siddhānti-yatiśa attained svarga by sanyasana-samādhi-vidhi . Becha-gauṇḍa, jord of Āvali in Jiḍḍuļige appears to have been her father while Bommara was the father-in-law and Kāmi-gauṇdi, the mother-in-law. The king is described as the lord of cities like Hastināpura and Vijayanagara and as aśvapati-gajapati-narapati-arirāya-vibhāḍa .

cells.date: Śaka 1268, Vyaya, Māgha-amāvāsye, Arkavāra, Śatabhisha, solar eclipse=1347 A.D., February 11
cells.object: On a single copper-plate in the possession of Maḍđi Śrinivāsāchārya, the  paṭēl .
cells.remarks: Records the gift of the village Kāntapuri renamed Vira Mārapapuri situated on the bank of the Varadā within Kamaṭhapura; in Nāgarakhaṇḍa of Eḍe-nāḍu of Chandragutti alias Gōmanta-parvata in Vanavāsi 12000, to 22 Bīāhmaṇas who were emigrants from Andhra country, by Mārappa, the prince ( yuvarāṭ ) who was ruling Chandragupti. He is said to have defeated the Kadamba king and gone to Gōkarṇa. Refers to the three ministers, Mādhava, Kriyāśakti and Triyambaka. Gods Virūpāksha and Madhukēśvara of Yaḍa-nāḍu are cited as witnesses.

cells.date: 1) Śaka 1370, Vibhava, Māgha ba. 11, Tuesday = 1449 A.D., February 18, f.d.t. .22
cells.object: On a pillar in front of the same temple.
cells.remarks: 2) Śaka 1371, Śukla, Jyēshṭha śu. 11, Tuesday, Anurādhā-nakshatra. Tulhi = 1449 A.D., June 2, Monday. The nakshatra was Svāti Records the consecration of the image of Vṛishabha in the temple of Rā.nayidēva and a grant of land for offerings to god Rāmadēva and burning a perpetual lamp before (god) Basavarāja on the second date by Viri-seṭṭi, Malli-seṭṭi and Honni-seṭṭi, sons of Sirumi-seṭṭi of Lāyadakere, resident of Hirīyakeṛe, the pṛithviseṭṭi of the 18 kampaṇas of Chandra-gutti, who came and lived in Koḍakaṇi when there was some disturbance ( maharājika ) on the death of king Dēvarāya on the first date. The gift land was made over, after purchase to Bommidēva the aṛiya (son-in-law) of Rāmayidēva, the priest, after celebrating his marriage and entrusting him with the maintenance of a feeding house and worship in the temple. The gift was made after worshipping Dhūpada-oḍeya of Kōpura, the pontiff of Sirumi-seṭṭi.

cells.object: On a stone in front of the Sadāśiva temple.
cells.remarks: Agaļabāgalu Damaged and broken. Records the reassignment of lands on the second date, among several Brāhmaṇas after recovering some of them which had not been properly assigned earlier. Refers to a grant made on the first date by Rāmarāja-nāyaka, probably the Keļadi chief. Rāmakṛīshṇappayya, son of mahānāyakāchārya Nārāyaṇappayya of gold treasury (?) chinna-bhaṇdāra ), was designated the chief yajamāna of the agrahāra village Sadāśivapura. Also records the grants of lands as vṛittis for the mahājans reciters of purāṇas and for the satra of the temple. etc.

Refers to a grant made on the first date by Rāmarāja-nāyaka, probably the Keļadi chief. Rāmakṛīshṇappayya, son of  mahānāyakāchārya  Nārāyaṇappayya of gold treasury (?)  chinna-bhaṇdāra ), was designated the chief  yajamāna  of the  agrahāra  village Sadāśivapura. Also records the grants of lands as  vṛittis  for the  mahājans  reciters of  purāṇas  and for the  satra  of the temple. etc.

cells.date: Śaka 1330, Sarvajit, Šrāvaṇa ba. 8, Thursday =1407 A.D., July 28. The Śaka year was current.
cells.object: Slab near the Durgā temple.
cells.remarks: Viṭhaṇṇa-vođeya (of Brahmakṣhatriya family) was governing Araga-rājya when Virupaṇṇa, son of Paṭanipāṭa Liṅgarasa, made over the village of Ālugavaļi of Jommāpura and some portions of Kauri to convert it into an agrahāra called Jommāpura and the lands divided into vrittis among several Brāhmaṇas named, free of several taxes etc Siṅgaṇṇa, the sēnabōva wrote the record which was endorsed by yajamāna Virupaṇṇa. Goddess Banadēvi is cited as a witness. Some more portion of the record (?) appears to have been engraved on the top; but it is damaged.

cells.date: Śaka 1327, Tāraṇa Mārgaśira, ba. 13, Saturday=1405 A.D., December 5
cells.object: On a stone near  śānabhōga  Subbarāya's wet land.
cells.remarks: Records a grant of land in the vijlage Kobađe in Rāū-nāḍu naming it Nāgalāpura after the mother of Kēśavadēva-heggađe and dividing it into 3 shares, to Virupaṇṇa. Kallappa and Māyaṇṇa sons and grandsons of Māyaṇṇa of Iñgalēśvara belonging to Ātrēya-gōtra and Ēik-śākhā. The grant was made with the consent of the prabhus of all the nāḍus of 18 kampaṇas of Āraga-vēṇthe, all the halaru of three cities, four mandus of Rāu-nāḍu and sixty villages and dānamūlis of Kobađe. Kēśavadēva-heggađe of Mālūru is described as the chief the mandus and 60 villages.

cells.remarks: Viruppa-voĵeya (son of Rāyappa) was governing the Āraga kingdom at the instance of the king. All the nāṇus of the 18 kampaṇas of Āraga-vēṇthe and the halaru of three cities unanimously agreed and made a gift of land rented at 12 honnu in the village Bondiya of Muduvaṅka-nāḍu, after purchase, as sarvamānya free from imposts like suṅka , kāruka , grāma-gadyāṇa , pañchakāruka etc., for the offerings of god Kalinātha of Āraga. Ends with the sign-manual of god Kalinātha of the mūlasthāna of Āraga.

cells.date: Śaka 1026, Tāraṇa, Kārttika śu. 1, Wednesday.  Tithi  = 1404 A.D., October 5, Sunday, the Śaka year being 1326.
cells.object: On the same stone.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Viṭthaṇṇa, son of Rāmappa-ođeyara Bommaṇṇa, who was protecting the Āraga kingdom, granted to god Mūlasthāna Kalinātha of Āraga, land having a fixed rent of 25 honnus in the village Bondiya of Muduvañka-nāđu of Āraga-vēṇthe, forming it into a village named Kalināthapura. This is said to be the writing of Viṭthaṇṇa. The Śaka year cited is definitely a mistake for 1326.

cells.date: Śaka 1326, Tāraṇa, Kārttika ba. 9, Monday = 1404 A.D., October 27
cells.object: Stone set up in front of the Banaśañkari temple.
cells.remarks: Damaged. It states that Viṭhaṇṇa son of Bommaṇṇāmātya made a gift of the village Mari-vari, renamed Chauđēśvaripuna in Muduvañika-nāđu of 18 kaṇpaṇas in Āraga-vēṇthe, which yielded 130 gadyāṇas from several levies, for the offerings of goddess Banadadēvi of Hiriyamgađi in Āraga. It was stipulated that daily worship should be performed in his name and specified dishes offered ( sēvageya pāyisa, ghārige, otsāvike, etc. ). Ananta-vajjhya son of Sōmaya-vajjhya who recited mahā-ākshaya stōtra was given 15 gas. Śrīsūkta was also to be recited, besides performing anointment etc.

cells.object: On a stone lying in front of the same temple.

cells.date: Śaka 1327, Pārthi[va], Śrāvaṇa śu. 1 = 1405 A.D., July 27, Monday
cells.object: Stone to the right of the Kalinātha temple.
cells.remarks: When Virappa-vođeya of the Brahmakshatra family was governing the Āraga-rājya the gauḍa-prabhus of Mandu-nāđu-30 and Muduvañka-nāđu-4 in the eighteen kampaṇas of Āraga, having assembled and agreed unanimously granted for god Mūlasthāna Kalinātha of Āraga land situated in the village Toragale, in the mēlubhāgi of Muduvañka-nāđu after purchase for 2 ga, for the perpetual lamp of the god. Sēnabōva Hariyappa of Āraga wrote the record. Virappa-vođeya is stated to have been the son of Brahmarāja of the Saṅkappa-Rāyappa family.

cells.date: Śaka 1386 ( rasa, ashṭa-guṇa-bhū ), Svabhānu, Vaiśākha, śu. 11, Friday = 1463 A.D., April 29. The Śaka year was current.
cells.object: On a set of 5 copper-plates of the Puttige-małha.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of the village Saraballige surnamed Gajabēte Dēvarāyapura, with its hamlet Haļļivāna in Niđuvalla-nāđu of Sāntalige-māgaṇi in Āraga-rājya to Dēvappa-daṇdanātha, eldest son of Śrigirinātha, governor of Āraga-rājya on the occasion of the naming ceremony ( nāmakaraṇōtsava ) of Dēvarāya, son of the king. The donee Dēvappa who was also the minister obtaining the permission of the king divided the agrahāra into 80½ shares and distributed them among 47 Brāhmaṇas. Viraṇa, son of Muddaṇāchārya, engraver of this inscription received one share. It ends with he sign-manual śrī Virūpā-ksha .

cells.object: On a stone in the backside of Mukundāchārya's house.
cells.remarks: . . . . . Fragmentary and damaged. Records the grant of lands in the village Bālagāra-kuppa within Bekkase, for the worship and offerings of god Rāma by Viraṇṇa-vođeya, and several seṭṭis etc. of a nāđu , (name lost) after purchase. A part of the gift appears to have been made over to Sulabhatīrtha-śrīpāda who was worshipping the deity (Rāma ?) at Bālagāra alias Ayōdhyāpura, w ithin Bekkase of Āragada-vēṇitheya. Several Brāhmaṇas (named) also received vrittis . A Sanskrit verse at the end offers obeisance to Trailōkyabhūshaṇa-yati, disciple ( putra ) of Mādhavārya-tirtha well-versed in Madhu-śāstra as propounded in Sudhā . Viraṇṇa-ođeya is said to be of the family of (son of ?) Rāyappa's Bommaṇṇa. Cf. KN 2079 above.

cells.remarks: 3 74 Damaged. When Sadāśivarāya-nāyaka (of Keļadi) was ruling the Āraga province, and by his order Šēšappa was protecting the same province, Krīshṇadēva of Ēik-śākhā and Kāśyapa-gōtra having consecrated god Lakshminārāyaṇa in Beļļagōđu-agrahāra alias Nara simhapura in the Aivattu-nāđu of the province the mahājanas of the agrahāra made a gift of lands for the offerings of that god and for the feeding house set up. It ends with the sign manual Śrī Vidyāśaṅkara .

cells.date: 1) Šaka 1329/1330 Sarvajit . . . . Monday =1407-08 A.D. ; 2) Sarvadhāri, Āśvija-amāvāsya, Friday =1408 A.D, October 19
cells.object: Stone in  Brahma-bana  of Sōma' yard.
cells.remarks: Broken and damaged. Registers a sale deed of land by all the nāđus of the 18 kampaṇas and three paṭṭaṇas to god Dakshiṇāmūrti, on the first date of the record when Rāyappođeya's V.ṭhaṇṇa was governing Āraga-rājya. It ends with the sign manual of god Kali-nātha of the mūlasthāna of Āraga. On the second date of the record Vairāgya Śivāchārya-dēva (the pontiff of the temple?) is stated to have converted (the gift lands) into an agrahāra called Dakshiṇāmūrti Śivāchāryapura and distributed the lands among several Brāhmaṇas named. Details are lost. The record refers to the rule of a Vijayanagara king whose name cannot be made out. It falls in the reign-period of Dēvarāya 1 of the Samgama family.

cells.remarks: First inscription of the village. Records the sale of lands in Beļali and Kittađūru to Viṭhappa, son of Bañkarasa of Kāśyapa-gōtra and Ēik-śākhā, under the agreement of nāđaprabhus of three cities of the Ā:aga 18 kampaṇas and Viṭhappa governor of the Āraga province. It seems to state that the donee paid va 75 hon towards the sūsina varaha (?) to the halaau of 18 kampaṇas and 3 paṭṭaṇas from out of the incomes like fixed revenue and customs. The total value of the land paid was 300 varaha honnu . This was written by Mallappa sēnabōva of Honnagauđi. Contains the sign-manual śri kalināthadēvaru .

cells.object: On a second inscription in the village.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of the two villages Beļali and Kittadūru farmed into an agrahāra re-named Akkāmbikāpura, after the donor's mother, dividing it into 22 shares, to a number of Brāhmaṇas of various gōtras and śākhās , by Viṭhappa, son of Bañkarasa(and Akkāyavve). cells.date: Šaka 1285, Šubhakṛit, Pushya = 1362 A.D., December-1363 A.D., January
cells.object: On a boulder in the filed of the  maṭha .
cells.remarks: Damaged and purport not clear. Seems to register a gift of 100 gadyāṇas due to the village named after himself as Virūpākshapura, subject to a deduction of 20 honnu of taxes. Mentions Virupaṇṇa ođeya. It refers to 50 Yađeha!li honnu 20 Bentula ga etc., these probably being the specified amounts due. A supplement refers to Virupaṇṇa-vođeya at whose instance some gift was made to the mahṇjanas . The king mentioned was a prince that did not rule, but assted his father in administration.

cells.date: Śaka 1322, Vikrama, Māgha ba. 2, Monday =1401 A.D., January 31, Monday, f.d.t. .02
cells.object: In a field of Survey No. 91.
cells.remarks: When Jannarasa-vođeya was protecting the Āraga province, Bomma-hegađe of Bikkava||i in Muduvańka-nāđu of Āraga-věnthe made a grant of land to Kěšappa, son of Dāmodara-nāyaka of Āṅgirasa-Bārhaspatya-Bhāradvāja-gōtra. Dāmodara-bhaṭṭa's son Kṛishṇappa also appears to have received some land. Several seṭṭis and heggađes are cited as witnesses. The inscription was written by Siṅgaṇṇa, the sēnabōva of the nāđu .

cells.date: Šaka 1329, Sarvajit, Šrāvaṇa ba. 1, Thursday=1407 A.D., July 21
cells.object: Stone in Hosakoppa-kānu.
cells.remarks: When kumāra Viṭhaṇṇođeya. of the Brahmakshatriya lineage of Sańkappa Rāyappa family, was ruling the Āraga province, a grant of lands in Halavanaha!ļi was made to Hadigala Kāmōja, son of Bideya Bommōja, by all (the members of) Mandanāđu-30 in Hombuchcha-nāđu-2, of the 18 kampaṇas of Āraga-rājya. Sēnabōva Bommarasa wrote the record. The donee was exempted from payment of taxes like biṭṭi, koṭṭaṇa and sollage and the land it self was inclusive of.wet land, dry land, makki, hakkalu, kummari, halasu, meṇasu and kedala-biļilu .

cells.date: Šaka 1327, Tārapa.. , Friday, lunar eclipse. Probably=1404 A.D., July 22, Tuesday, Šaka year being current.
cells.object: Slab in a field to the south of the village.
cells.remarks: Damaged. When Vithappa-ođeya was governing probably the Āraga province all the nāđu (of Hombucha-nāđu ?) having agreed upon, made a grant of a village (name not clear) and probably other lands to Nāgaṇna, son of Hulagila Nāgaṇna, of Ēik-šākhā, free of all encumberances and taxes like sumka-kāruka , grāmia-gadyāna , pañcha-kāruka , oļavari , horavari , taļasārika , aledere , tōṭadere , etc. Mallappa, the sēnabōva of Hombuchcha-nāđu wrote the record which was endorsed by all the gauđas . cells.date: Šaka 1298, Naļa, Māgha ba. 30, Monday. solar eclipse. The eclipse occurred in Pushya, Saturday, January 10 of 1377 A.D. Cited  tithi  = February 8, Sunday.
cells.remarks: The stone in the hasanakallu-hakkalu . Damaged. When Vira Bukkarāya's son Virupaṇṇa-ođeya of Udagiri was ruling the Āraga kingdom, all the gauđa-praje made a gift of the village Huttadahaļli in their nāđu with all rights, to Virupaṇṇa-vođeya's house-hold minister Rāmarasa. Rāmarasa formed it into an agrahāra renamed Hariharapura and dividing it into twentytwo shares bestowed them upon Bīāhmaṇas whose names are given. It ends with the sign-manual śri Kallinātha-dēvaru .

cells.date: Šaka 1327 [Pār]thiva . . . . = 1405-05 A.D.
cells.object: Stone in a field.
cells.remarks: Registers a grant of land of the sowing capacity of 17 khaṇđugas and tenancy value of 2 kuļas in the hamlet attached to Koļavaļi Kukari in Maravaļige-nāđu of Sātaļige-nāđu in Āraga-vēnthe to Vāmarasa, son of Sōyidēva and probably grandson of Urilnūgada Vāmarasa, of Bādarāyaṇa-gōtra and Ēik-śākhā by the mahāprabhus and mahājanas of the nine agrahāras in the presence of god Virabhadra of Āraga- Sēnabōva Naraharidēva wrote the record. The name of the ođeya who was governing Āraga-rājya is lost. It is attested by all the nāđus of Sātaļige and has the sign-manual of Kēšava Śriṅganāthadēva.

cells.date: Šaka 1291, Saumya, Kārttika śu. 1, Thursday =1369 A.D., October 2, Tuesday
cells.object: Stone set up in the garden of Puṭṭasāmaiah.
cells.remarks: Refers to mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Sōvaṇṇa-vođeya, son of Vira Mārappa-vođeya who made a grant of certain lands in Jegaṭigāru in Muduvańka-nāđu to Dēvaṇṇa-bhaṭṭa, son of Nāraṇa-bhaṭṭa of Hārita-gōtra. Mārappa-vođeya is the youngest brother of Bukka I and Sōvaṇṇa his son. Although the record does not refer to his rule, this may be assigned to Bukka I.

cells.date: Śaka 1284, Subhakṛit, Māgha śu. 5, Thursday.  Tithi  = 1363 A.D., January 20, Friday
cells.object: On a stone in the Kallu-basti.
cells.remarks: Records the fixation of the boundaries of the lands belonging to the Pārśvadēva temple of Taṭatāla in Heddūranāđu, by the ministers Nāgaṇṇa and Dēvarasa as also Jaina Mallappa, after enquiring the halaru of the three cities and the 18 kampaṇas , who were summoned to the Āraga-chāvađi. This fixation was made consequent upon a dispute between the people of Heddūra-nāđu and the temple āchāryas and sūris Viruppaṇṇa-vođeya, son of the king was ruling Male-rājya. Contains an eulogy of Chārukīrti-paṇđita of Mula-saṅgha, Dēsi-gaṇa, Pustaka-gachchha and Koṇđakundāñvaya.

cells.date: Śaka 1386 ( rasa, ashṭa, guṇa, bhū ), Svabhānu, Vaiśākha śu. 11, Friday = 1463 A.D., April 29. The Śaka year was current.
cells.object: On a set of 5 copper-plates received from the Puttige-maṭha.
cells.remarks: Records a grant of the village Sarabaļige ( alias Gajabeṭtē-Dēvarāyapura) in Niđuvalla-nāđu, belonging to Sāntalige-māgaṇi, of Āraga-mahārājya to Dēvapāmātya, son of Śrigi-rinātha, in the occasion of the naming ceremony ( nāmakaraṇa-mahōtsava ) of Dēvarāya. Dēvapāmātya, with the consent of the king divided the village into 80½ vṛittis and best-owed them to a number of Brāhmaṇas (whose names are given). Viraṇa, son of Muddaṇā-chārya, the engraver, received one vṛitti .

cells.date: Śaka 1325, Svabhānu, Phālguṇa ba. 5, Sunday = 1404 A.D., March 2
cells.object: Stone set up near the Basavanakallu.
cells.remarks: Registers a grant of the village Kaūdavaļļi alias Virupāmbikāpura in Beļuveya-nāđu of Āraga-vēņthe, to Viiṭavappa, son of Rāghavadēva Āchappa of Śrīvatsa-gōtra, and Ēik-śākhā, by the halaru of 3 cities, all the nāđu of the 18 kumpaṇas of Āraga-vēņthe who paid 95 varaha ga towards uṁbaļi, hombaļi, suṅka, kāruka and grāmagadyāṇa . Siṅgaṇṇa, the sēnabōva of Muduvaṅka-nāđu wrote the record. Viiṭhappa-ođeya of the lineage of Saṅk-appa Rāyappa belonging to Brahmakshatriya family, who was governing the Āraga province is described as a devotee of Kriyāśakti-guru and worshipper of the feet of (god) Triyambaka. His mother was Virupāmbikā.

cells.date: Šaka 1328, Pārthiva, Bhādrapada ba... = 1405 A.D., October
cells.object: Stone in the  hakkalu  of the village.
cells.remarks: Damaged and details lost. When Viṭhaṇṇa-ođeya of the Brahmakshatriya family, of the lineage of Saṅkappa-Rāyappa and son of Brahmarāja was governing Āraga-rājya, and while Narasimhabhāratītirtha-śripāda was the pontiff of Śriṅgēri, the gauḍu-praje sold the village Kesare for 160 varaha ga after deducting 22 (?) towards tenancy ( kulā ) as mēluvadike and also probably some land (?) in Iđagere for 15 varaha ga , together for 175 varaha ga to Mallapa (Mal'i-bhiṭṭa), son of Koṅgaṇa-upādh/āya of Śriṅgēri, belonging to Dhanañjaya-Viśvāmitra-gōtra and Sāma-Śākhā. He converted it into an agrahāra named Narasimhabhāratipura and distributed the lands therein to several Brāhmaṇas. One vritti was gifted to god Vidyāśaṅkara of Śriṅgēri. The gauḍa-prajes were from Mandu-nāḍu and Hombuchcha-nāḍu 2 wiṭhin 18 Kaṭpaṇas of Āraga-vēṇṭhe.

cells.date: Śaka 1354 (expired), Paridhāvi (current), Mārgaśira, ba. 2, Wednesday.  Tithi  = 1432 A.D.
cells.object: On the hero-stone in the Māsti temple.
cells.remarks: December 9 Tuesday When Sirigirínātha-ođeya, son of Rāyappa-ođeya of the Brāhmakshatriya family was governing the Āraga kingdom, Putta-[he]gađe (?) son of Bommarasa-heggađe died while fighting with the paṭhavāḥi at Koļavaḥi in Šātaļige-nāđu. The deceased's father made a gift of land to jōyisa Siñgaṇṇa, in memory of the deceased. The valour of the deceased is said to have reminded one of Kumāra Rāmanātha. The hero-stone was sculptured by Virōja, son of Sūrōja.

cells.date: 1) Šaka 1316, Bhāva, Šrāvaṇa ba. 5, Sunday=1394 A.D., August 16, (Nija Srāvaṇa);
cells.object: On a boulder in a field.
cells.remarks: 2) Prabhava, Āśvija śu. 10, Thursday, Dhaṇishtha. The tithi =1387 A.D., September 23, Monday, f.d n. .37 Damaged. Sōvaṇṇa-vođeya is stated to be governing Āraga-rājya. cells.object: Stone near  Brahmanakaṭte .

cells.date: Śaka 1339, Hēmalambi, Śrāvaṇa ba.10, Sunday=1417 A.D., August 7, Saturday
cells.object: Stone in  lakkibīlalu .
cells.remarks: Viṭhaṇṇa-voḍeya, son of Brahmadēva-oḍeya of Brahmakshatriya family was governing Āraga-rājya. Nāgaṇṇa-heggaḍe, his brothers Balla-heggaḍe, Tamma-heggaḍe (?), aļiya Baīchaṇṇa-heggaḍe and all the members of the family of Mēgaravalīli in Madavaļige-nāḍu, within Sātaļige-nāḍu of Āraga-vēnṭhe together agreed and sold the land and arecanut trees below the tank at Mumbaļe and at Lokavalīli, for 42 hons and 5 haṇas (42½ hons ), to Dēva-rpayya, son of Nāgappayya, worshipper of god Viśvēśvara and belonging to the lineage of Upēndrāchārya, of Ātrēya-gōtra and Sāma-Śākhā and others named. Sēnabōva Bammarasa wrote the record attested by several persons. Ends with the sign-manual of (gods) Sañka-radēva and Mailāradēvi.

cells.date: 1) Viśvāvasu, Jyēshṭha śu. 10, Friday =1605 A.D., May 17 2) Śaka 1530, Saumya, Māgha śu. 10, Sunday =1610 A.D., January 24, Wednesday, the Śaka year being 1531.
cells.object: Stone in the  raṅgamaṇṭapa  of Ādināthasvāmi-basti.
cells.remarks: Āraviṣu: Veṅkaṭapati ruling from Penugoṇḍa States that Bommaṇa śeṭti Padumaṇa-śeṭti, Chandana-śrēshṭi, Māṇika-śrēshṭi and Ādaṇṇa, the five sons of Bommaṇa and Nēmāmbā, had the Anantanātha-chaityālaya god built by their grandfather Bommaṇa-śrēshṭi, son of Vardhamāna and Nēmāmbā on the first date noted above, reconstructed in stone and had Ananta-tirthēśvara consecrated therein on the second date. For worship, offerings etc. in the chaityālaya originally Bommaṇa-heggaḍe of Muttūru, belonging to Gaṅgara-baļi had made a grant of 12 khaṇḍugas of land in the village Nelugāra. For this some more lands etc. were added as gifts by the brothers. It states that Veṅkaṭādri-nāyaka was governing the city of Āraga, to the east of Bhuvaṇa-giri in Āvani-dēśa and that Bommaṇa-heggaḍe was administering Muttūru as his hereditary tenant ( kuļa kālāmchi ). The basadi was situated in Mēļige in Kōdūrapālu in Niṣuvala-nāṣu of Muttūru (?)-sime. The record also registers gifts of land, arecanut trees etc. some of them after purchase, by other individuals. The pontifical genealogy of the preceptors of Bommaṇa-seṭti is given as follows : Vidyānanda-muni, Dēvēndrakirti-bhatṭāraka Abhinava Viśālatkirti-bhatṭāraka of Balātkāra-gaṇa.

cells.date: Śaka 1326, Tāraṇa, Āśvayuja śu. 11, Monday =1404 A.D., September 15
cells.object: Slab in front of the Hariharēśvara temple.
cells.remarks: Top portion is damaged. States that the king having passed away, for his merit, his minister Viṭhaṇṇa-oḍeya who was governing Āraga kingdom converted the village Mukta Hariharapura into an agrahāra and having received several lands and money incomes as donations from the people of Bēlūru in Muduvańka-nāđu of Āraga-venthe, distributed it among several Brāhmaṇas of the newly created agrahāra . It further states that in the month of Kārttika ba. 30, (November 3, Monday of 1404 A.D.,) Bōgāra Heggi-setīti, a devotee of Kālikādēvi and Kamaṭhēśvaradēva had the Śaiva goldsmiths, carpenters and blacksmiths settled in the village to serve the mahājanas and exempted them from the payment of kāṇike , hađapagāṇike , bitīti , bidāra , uđugo xe , volupa , etc. The record was written by Viraṇṇa.

cells.date: Śaka 1301, Siddhārthi, Kārttika śu. 1, WednesJay = 1379 A D., October 12.
cells.object: Stone by the side of the Kallēśvara temple.
cells.remarks: It refers to the rule of Virupaṇṇa-ođeya of Vudageri (Udayagiri ?), son of Bukkarāya and states that all the gauđa-praje (some of whom are named) of Hombuchcha-nāđu-2 and Manda-nāđu-30 and the five n.ūlīgas of Niṭṭūru agreeing among themselves, gave a charter to Bokkasada Mallappa undertaking to pay 12 ga to the palace besides levies like heṇṇuļi kāṇike , etc., and 14 ga to Mallappa annually and enjoy the land bestowed on them as mūlasyāmis . Dēvappa, the nāđasēnabōva , wrote the record to which several attested as witnesses.

cells.date: Saka 1346, Subhakṛit, Chaitra śu. 1, Sunday, solar eclipse. Irregular.  Tithi  = 1422 A.D., March 23, Monday. No such eclipse occurred either in Subhakṛit (Saka 1344) or Sōbhakṛit (Saka 1345).
cells.remarks: The stone (second) fixed in front of a maṭha . States that Gaṅgādharapuri-śripada, disciple of Dēvēndrapuri-śripāda of Tīrthadahaļļi purchased land in the village Hennaṅgi, a hamlet of Bukkarājapura from Rāmaṇṇa, son of Subrahmaṇya-bhaṭṭa and Chennamāmbā and grandson of Nāgupādhyāya of Bukkarājapura and gifted it for the feeding house. It further states that his junior pontiff Īśvara-svarūpa-[śrī ?]pāda having died of blood jaundice ( rakta-hatarāgi muktarādalli ) arrangements were made for feeding 8 Brāhmaṇas in his name, one Brāhmaṇa in the name of his teacher and 2 Brāhmaṇas in his own name besides, paddy and money due from several towards interest received on the loans on hedges of lands were also gifted. Saṅkarapuṭṭa was the manager of the feeding house. Sirigirināthadēva is stated to have been administer-ing Āraga-rājya.

cells.object: On a set of 9 copper-plates.
cells.remarks: Records the re-assignment of lands among several Brāhmaṇas on the second date, after recovering some of them which had not been properly assigned earlier. It refers to an earlier grant made on the first date. The record states that formerly during the rule of Sadāśivarāya, pradhāna Mādappayya established an agrahāra on the bank of the Kuśāvati in the name of his master Sadāśivarāya-nāyaka of Keṭadi who was governing Gutti, Āraga, 18 kampaṇas , Bārakūru and Mangalūru. The new village named Sadāśivapura, to the east of Virūpa-samudra of Araga had been formed after purchasing lands around belonging to the mahājanas of 60 agrahāras and there in Śīva and Vishṇu temples had been constructed. But there had been some confusion. Some Brāhmaṇas had built houses and settled while some others had not. Therefore, during the rule of the present king, on the first date when Rāmarāya-nāyaka of Keṭadi was governing, things were set right by making gift of some more lands. Rāmakṛishṇappayya, son of Nārāyaṇappayya of Chinna-bhanṭāra , belonging to Vaśishṭa-gōtra, Aśvalāyana sūtra and Rik-śākha, was designated as the chief ( yajamāna ) of the agrahāra village. This was further re-assigned on the second date and several re-adjustments made.

cells.date: Śaka 1343, Plava, Śrāvaṇa śu 5=1421 A.D., July 5, Saturday if intercalary and August 3, Sunday if it is regular month of Śrāvaṇa.
cells.object: Stone in the courtyard of the  małha .
cells.remarks: Registers a sale-deed of land in Haṅgara-bayalu within Hiriya-Hołalūru, by Nāgaṇṇa-hebbāruva and Bommarasa-hebbāruva, sons of Nāgappa-hebbāruva and others named who were the mahājanas of that place (Hiriya Hołalūru) for 44 varaha ga which was the current price and 4 varaha ga being the uđugore (in all 48 varaha ga ), to Śaṅkarabharati-śripāda, the pontiff of the małha at Tirthamuttūru in Kełabhāgi of Sāntaļige in Āraga-vēņthe. Śrigirināthadēva, son of Bommāṇṇa and grandson of Rāyappa-vođeya (?) of Brahmakshatriya family was governing Āraga-rājya. The sale of land was inclusive of the asiṭabhōgas and (incomes f. o u) betelnu., mango, māni , kummari , kōhu and along with dāni-mūli salike and avadhi (?) Naraharidēva, the sēnubōva of Sāntaļige-nāđu wrote the record. Several individuals are cited as signatories and witnesses.

cells.object: Stone in the forest.
cells.remarks: . . . . . 12, Thursday Fragmentary and worn out. Registers the sale of three villages for 350 hons to Viṭṭhaṇṇa-vođeya who is described as a mantri belonging to the family of Santapa-Rāyappa. He converted them into an agrahāra named Virupāmbikāpura and gifted 2 vrittis of land therain to god Virūpāksha and the remaining 30 vrittis to many Brāhmaṇas. cells.date: Śaka 1317 ( sapta-ehandra-agni-vidhu ) Bhāva. Āshāḍha śu. 12.  Tīthi =1394 A.D., June 11, Thursday. The Śaka year was 1316.
cells.object: On a set of 3 copper-plates in the possession of Kollara-bhaṭṭa.
cells.remarks: Records the grant of a village Virūppāpura with its 10 hamlets (named) in Śrirangapaṭṭa-ṇa-rājya, in the Tungabhadrā-dēśa containing 44 shares to a number of Brāhmaṇas of various gōtras and śākhas , and also to the gods of the village (3 shares) for god Virūpāksha of Pampā (2 shares) and to Sōmanātha, son of Sirigirinātha (1 share). Also records the grant of dasavanda of 4 khaṇḍugas of rice-field and 1000 areca trees to Sōmanātha-voḍeya. This was engraved by the order of the sculptor śasanāchārya Nāgidēva.

cells.object: On a set of 5 copper-plates in the possession of  purāṇika  Narasimha-bhaṭta.
cells.remarks: The king made a grant of the village Lakhumāpura alias Kṛishṇadēvamahārāya-samudram in Būdihāla-sime belonging to Magare-nāḍa-vēṇṭheya, to Lakshmīdhara-bhaṭta, son of Kṛishṇa-bhaṭta of Āśvalāyana-sūtra, Prathama Atrēya-gōtra, and Rik-śākhā, in the presence of god Virūpāksha, on the bank of the Tuṅgabhadrā. Ends with the sign-manual śri Virū-pāksha .

cells.date: Šaka 1306, Raktākshi, Šrāvaṇa šu. 12, Vađđavāra =1384 A.D., July 30, Saturday

text.remarks: Records the remission of all taxes like  siddhāya, kāṇike, birāđa, bijavari  etc., payable on the lands belonging to the temples of Mallikārjuna, Bhīmēśvara and Vighnēśvara for the worship and offerings of the same gods, by Siṅgappa-nāyaka described as the 'dear son' of the king. The lands 24½  kha  of wet land, two gardens and dry land – had been gifted earlier.

cells.date: Šaka 1511 ( (bhū, šašānka, šara, kshōni) ) Sarvadhāri, Māgha šu. 15, eclipse. A solar eclipse occurred in the cyclic year on 1589 A.D., February 4, Tuesday, while a lunar eclipse occurred in the previous year Sarvajit on Monday, 1588 A.D., January 29.
cells.object: On a set of 7 copper-plates in the possession of Rāma-bhaṭta.
cells.remarks: Recounts the genealogy of the king. Registers a royal grant of a village Šravaṇagere, otherwise called Tirumalapuri, in Huļēru-sīme belonging to Magara-nāđa-vēnṭhe of Hoyi-saṇa-rājya, to several Brāhmaṇas of many šākhās, gōtras and sūtras (named) The verses of this inscription were composed by Křishṇakavi Kāmakōṭi, Sabhāpati's grand son and was engraved by Gaṇapa's son Viraṇa-mahāchārya.

cells.date: Šaka 1591, Saumya, Chaitra šu. 1, Saumyavāsara=1669 A.D., March 22, Monday. The Kannada text gives the Šaka year as 1651=1729 A.D., March 19, Wednesday.
cells.object: On a copper-plate in the possession of Lakshmīnārāyaṇa-šāstri.
cells.remarks: It records a grant of the village Apehalli in Hāgalavāđi-sthala to Rāmayya, son of Chennayya and grandson of Yaddanapūđi Peraņeya Timmaiya, of Bhāradvāja-gōtra, Āpas-tamba-sūtra and Yajuś-śākhā by Mudiyappa-nāyakarayya, son of Chennabasavappa-nāyaka, grandson of Sāli-nāyaka of Gāūla-gōtra to whom the king favoured the village Yareya-kaṭta in the Hoysala-sime for his permanent chieftaincy ( amaranāyakatana .) A maṭha having been newly erected in the grove at Apehalli which had been already granted to Rāmayya, some land in the gift village was taken over in lieu of which the donor gave the donee the right of utilisation of water from the Hāgalavāđi tank for irrigating one khaṇđuga of rice-land ( Jirigemađu-guade ).

cells.date: Šaka 1544, Dundubhi, Māgha ba. 14-1623 A.D., February 18
cells.object: On a stone in the Daļavāyi-maṭha.
cells.remarks: Records that Kanāda šīlavanta daļavāyi Paramappa built a maṭha , excavated a tank and raised a garden and granted them to Nandišvarasvāmi. cells.date: Śaka 1392, Vikriti, Jyēsṭha ba. 7, Wednesday=1470 A.D., May 22, Tuesday. The Śaka year is read as 1272 in the Kannada text.
cells.object: On a stone in front of the Mallikārjuna temple.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Refers to an earlie grant made on the date of the record and states that when mahāpradhāna Siñgappa-daṇṇāyaka was administering, a mahāsāmanta and mahāmanneya (name lost) and his wife Kallarasiyamma renovated the Mallikārjuna temple, constructed the bāgila-pađasāle , bhōga-maṇṭapa , śikhara-paṭasāle and made a gift of some lands for the service of Sidda Mallikārjuna. It mentions sthānika Sōmayyadēva and his sister Honnidēvi ; hāđuva Mahādēvi, tāļada Mākajji were the basavis of the god. The record was written by Ballehada Malla. There are a few verses in the beginning in praise of god Mallikārjuna of Śrīgiri.

cells.date: Šaka 1585, Krōdhi, Kārttika śu. 2, Tulā-saṅktamaṇa=1564 A.D., October 11, the Šaka year being 1586. But the said  saṅkramaṇa  occurred on September 30.
cells.object: On two pieces of a stone near the  kaṭte .
cells.remarks: It registers a grant of a village Kaggere in Kuñigaļa-sthaļa for the services of god Tonṭada Siddēśvara of Kaggere by Dēvarāja-vađēraiyya, son of Dēvarāja-vođeya and grandson of Rāja-vođeya of Maisūru to celebrate the victory in the battle against the Ikkēri people. Daļavāyi Nandināthaiya was sent to face the battle-array. This is an important record throwing light in the political relations of the Vijayanagara king vis a vis the chief of Ikkēri and the rulers of Mysore.

cells.object: On a stone in the village.
cells.remarks: It records a gift of 30 kha of dry land and 30 kha of wet land below Diḍḍakere, converted into 16 vṛittis in the village Vēṇkaṭakṛishṇa-sāgara, newly established to the west of Kuṇigal, to several Brāhmaṇās (named) made by Veṇkaṭakṛishṇājamma, wife ( puṇya strī ) of Immaḍi Hirikempayya-gauḍa of Chaturtha-gōtra the chief of Elahaṇka-nāḍu. cells.date: Śaka 1302, Raudri, Mārgaśira śu. 1, Monday. The month cited was a leap month. The  tithi =1380 A.D., October 29, Monday in Nija Kārttika.
cells.object: On a set of 3 copper-plates in the possession of Kālēnahalīli Sūra-bhaṭṭa.
cells.remarks: King's younger brother Vira Mallappa-ođeyar's son Channapa conquered the Turushkas who were swarming over Ādavāni-durga and the kingdom and took possession of the fort and kingdom, which he gave to Harihararāya. This Chennappa-ođeya granted the village Sige-māvina-halīli in Herūru-sthaṭa to Vēdamūrthi-upādhya's son Vidyābhūshana-dikshita as ekabhōg,a agrahāra , for his own happiness. Vidyābhūshana divided the village into 15 shares and gave them to various Brāhmaṇas (named). Ends with the sign-manual śri Virū-pāksha . The donor is said to have attested the record.

cells.date: Śaka 1508 (expressed by the chronogram  danti-vyōma-bhūta-indu ) Vyaya, Vaiśākha ba. 12 = 1586 A.D., May 5, Thursday
cells.reference: KSPP., Vol. XXI, pt. I, pp. 53 ff
cells.remarks: Set of 5 copper-plates in the possession of T.S. Gundurao. Registe's the renewal. by the king, of an original grant of the villages Juñjanahalli and Tārēhalli in Kōlāla-sime which were together formed into one village Puṭṭa-samudra, made by Kṛishṇadēvarāya in Śaka 1448 ( vasu-vēda-payōdhi-indu ), Vyaya, Vaiśākha. to Puṭṭayāmātya. To this Veñkaṭapati, to the king added another village named Huruligere in Chākigere-sime and made it over to Vāsarādhiśa,(son ?) of Puṭṭayāmātya. The gift is said to have been made at the instance of Hāvati Bhairava, son of Bhairavēadu-mahipāla and grandson of Mōlē Bhairava. Gaṇapayāchārya, son of Viraṇa, engraved the record. The text does not appear to have been proparly read.

cells.date: Śaka 1578. Durmukhi, Śrāvaṇa śu. 15, Bhaumavāra, lunar eclipse.=1656 A.D., July 26 Saturday and no eclipse The text in Kannada gives the Śaka date as 1698.
cells.remarks: Copy of a copper-plate in the possession of Pāñchāla Nāgalingappa. Records gifts of lands and money incomes for worship, offerings, etc. in the temples of by Kālīka, Kamaṭēśvara and Durgā and for maintaining Tippayya, who built the temple, Dođđa Raṇabhaire-gauđa of Hołavanahaļli, son of Raṇabhaire-gauđa and grandson of, Raṇabaiche-gauđa of Chaturtha-gōtra who was governing Hołavanahaļli Koraṭagere-vaļita. The record stipulates the amount of money to be paid by each house hold, annually, of the professional pāñchāla , nagartta , bēhāri , bōgāra , dēvaṅga , halepaika etc. all of whom unanimously agreed to pay. It also registers a gift of Agrahāra, a hamlet of Arasīpura in Koraṭagere-vaļita for goddess Durgā Mahēśvari by the chief. The record says that it is a record on paper ( kāgadada dāna-śāsana ) which had been got engraved (earlier) on a copper-plate. It refers to the coin duđđu . The genuineness of the record is doubtful.

cells.date: 1) Śaka 1369 ( nava-ritu-guṇa-bhū ), Prabhava, Mārgaśira śu. 12  godvādaśi  = 1447 A.D., November 19, Sunday 2) Śaka 1444, Chitrabhānu, Pushya śu. 1 = 1222 A.D., December 18 Thursday
cells.object: On a set of 3 copper-plates in the possession of Subrahmanya-śāstri.
cells.remarks: King Mallikārjuna granted the village Nallañji in the Bāyapa-hōbaļi belonging to Rāyadurga-rājya, renamed Dēvarāyapura, whose rēkhā was 200 varahas , to Adityarāya (who was the author of Bhāshyabhūshā , in the presence of god Chandramauli, on the first date. The donee was the son of Virūpākshārya of Bhāradvāja-gōtra, Bahvṛicha-śākhā, and well-versed in Sāṅkhya and Mīmāṁsa. On the second date Ādityadēva's grandsons, agreeing among themselves, petitioned to Chinna-mahādēvi, queen of Kṛṣhṇarāya, that the villages originally obtained from Immađi Dēva-mahārāya by their grandfather was in ruins, The queen made the village sarvamānya . Then, they divided the village into 70 vriitis , retained 20 for themselves and gave 20 for god Śrīraṅga of Śrīraṅga-samudra, 20 for Kēśava-sōmayāji, son of Basavā-bhaṭṭa, 2 for Viṭhala, the rāyasasvāmi , son of Rāmakṛṣhṇa, 2 for Mallaṇa, son of Viraṇāchārya, the engraver of the inscription and for Dugaya, the composer of the record.

cells.date: Śaka 1012, Sādhāraṇa, Chaitra śu. 5, Budhavāra Irregular.
cells.remarks: Copy of a copper-plate in the possession of Patel Mallayya. Āvala Kurubarāyaḍu and his 7 sons (named) paid a visit to the king Bukka-bhūpati, Buṭalirāya and Dēvarāya taking with them 1201 of their people, 7 herds of cows, 7 flocks of sheep, 6 carts of presentation cloths and a cartful of money. They presented to the king 7 times as much money as kāvaḍi will hold. They then went to the Araṇḍa forest on the instruction of the king and inscriptions of grants were set up in the Virūpāksha temple at Hampe, on the basement of the Kalikādēvi temple at Kanchi, on the Kuranji gate of Gutti, on a rock to the east of Baṅgāranāḍu in Penugoṇḍa. By the order of Dēvarāya, Vaḍḍi Hanumāna-bōyiḍu and others sent for the 60 families of their kinsmen and found 3 villages, made a tank and planted gardens near Hōmaguṇḍa. Money spent on this and certain temples is 1150 Rāmaṭeṅki-varahas , 1160 putali-kāsus , 3150 varahas . They then sent for the rulers and officials of the surrounding countries, brought there Murugāla Muttappa. the family guru and Tirumala-gauḍa went to Penugoṇḍa and brought Tirumalāchārya and consecrated the villages Nakārupaṭṇa, Māsināyana-baṇḍlu, Nāgapuripaṭṇa (also called Nāgalāpura) presented gifts to the gurus and set up inscriptions. A clear sorgery. Cf. No, KN 2209 above.

cells.date: 1) Saka 1592, Sādhāraṇa, Jyēshṭha śu. 12 = 1670 A.D., May 2) Vikrama, Kārttika ba. = 1700 A.D., November.
cells.object: On the second stone in the Kālahastiśvara temple.
cells.remarks: Harati Timmēndra considering Kālabasti-liṅga temple, set up by Rāmabhadra, as old, having consulted trusted men, ordered to renovate it. The sculptors erected a raṅga-maṇṭapa , chandraśāle and a stone pillar according to the directions given by Timmēndra. Records that mahānāyakāchārya Harati Timmaṇṇa-nāyaka made the grant of some lands for the offerings of god Kālabastiśvara, for the merit of the father and forefathers. It gives an account of the chief's family. A supplement added on the second date records a renewal of the grant of villages Doṭēri, Sireha, Tāvaregere, Hiriyāru, Ayimaṅgala and Niḍugallu-durga to Vira Hoṭṭaṇṇa-nāyaka of Harati by the king Veṅkaṭapatirāya.

cells.remarks: Mahānāyakāchārya Vira Timma the Harati chief set up the linga of Ārūṣhēśvara in the temple consecrated for that purpose to the south of the town of Kālāñjanagini, got excavated a tank and a pond, raised a garden and granted some lands in the Nyāyadaguṇte village for the service of the god. A supplement added on the second date states that Veñkaṭapatirāya renewed the chieftaincy over Doṣdēri, Siraha, Tāvaregere, Hiriyūru, Ayimaṅgala and Niṣugallu fort to Vira Hoṭṭeṇṇa-nāyaka.

cells.date: 1) Saka 1307 (expressed by the chronogram  adri-kha-vahni-chandra ), Krōdhana, Srāvaṇa śu. 15, lunar eclipse=1385 A.D., July 22, Saturday 2) Prabhava, Jyēshṭha, solar eclipse=1387 A.D., June 16, Sunday.
cells.object: On a set of 5 copper-plates in the possession of Krīshṇa-śāstrī.
cells.remarks: Contains a genealogical account. On the first date, nāyakāchārya Bommaṇa, younger brother of Kāmaṇa and son of Abē-nāyaka and Lakama-nāyiki made a grant of a village named Bukkarājapura to the Brāhmaṇas who, with their own funds constructed a tank near Nilugallu, across the river Banjehaļļa where it united with the stream Mosaļe between Kōtekere and Rāyadurga, at his instance. On the 2nd date these Brāhmaṇas approached Vijaya Bhūpati thinking that he would be the future king and got a charter from him, obviously confirming the earlier grant. The grant is attested by the sign-mannual of the prince: Rāmanātha .

cells.date: Šaka 1533, Virōdhikṛit, Phālguṇa šu. 13 = 1612 A D., March 5
cells.object: On the wall to the north of the Gōpalakrishṇa temple.
cells.remarks: Mudi-gauđa claimed the office of nāđagauđike by producing a false document ( kaṭā-vōle ) purported to have been issued by king Viraballā! in the past. But this was proved to be a falso vōle by the men sent from the palace to enquire into the affair when the office was bestowed upon Ānegonđa Kariṇigappa whereupon Mudi-gauđa disputed it. The office was thereafter once again bestowed upon Kariṇigappa in the presence of Mūle-ayya (the pontiff ?) of the temple of Bālakṛishṇa of Mēļikunṭe. It has the approval Immađi Rañ-gappa-nāyaka, the chief Harati.

cells.date: Siddhārthi, Bhādrapada, śu. 5, Monday=1379 A.D., August 18, Thursday
cells.object: On a copper-plate in the possession of  patēl  Dođđa Virabhadrē-gauđa.
cells.remarks: This is a charter issued by the king who, pleased with Nāgi-setĵi (and ?) Kāmi-setĵi, sons of Viśvanātha-setĵi of Eleyūru, granted them a palanquin, grāma-gadyāṇa of Sattige near Kaĵasa and exempted them from payment of several commercial taxes. It was laid down that they were entitled to certain privileges in the places wherever they went for business. They were also to sit upon judgement over matters of dispute between the several samayas of the dēśa . Ends with the sign-manual śri Virūpāksha .

text.remarks: The king granted 10  vṛittis  of land to Pāṇduramārya, son of Nṛisimhadāsa of Āśvalāyanasūtra and Vaśishṭha Bahavṛicha, renowned as a Hoysaṇīya, 8 other  vṛittis  to 8 other Brāhmaṇas (named, of whom 3 were Hoyasaṇīyas , 2 Kannaḍiyas, 1 a Kamme, 1 a Baḍaganāḍika and 1 a Mulikināḍiya) making altogether 18  vṛittis  at Treliṅganapālaka, surnamed Srinivāsapuri.

text.remarks: Damaged Mentions Jagannāthayadēva-mahārāja, son of  mahāmaṇdalēsvara  Dēvappa . . . . dāśigarāja of Ātrēyasa-gōtra, Āśvalāyana-sūtra.

cells.date: Śaka 1493, expressed by the chronogram  guṇa-nidhi vēda-in'lu , Prajōtpatti, Kārttika, śu. utthāna dvadāśi, Monday=1571 A.D., October 29.
cells.object: On a set of 7 copper-plates in the possession of Kestūru Srinivasacharya.
cells.remarks: Records a royal grant of the village Mallasamudra, also known as Timmasamudra in Ānebiddajari sthāna, belonging to Gūlūru-sime of Marugula-nāđu, in Hastināvati-va'lita of Penugoṇđa-rājya to a number of Brāhma'nas forming it into 100 v'ittis . The gift was made on the application of Mumma'i Timmappa-nāyaka, son of Kereyūru Imma'i Timma-nāyaka. Composer of this grant was Svayambhū, son of Sabhapati and the engraver Virayya Gaṇapāchārya.

cells.date: Śaka 1465, Śōbhakṛit, Āshāḥha ba. 3 = 1543 A.D.: June 19, Tuesday
cells.object: On a stone in the south wall of the Raṅganātha temple.
cells.remarks: Records the remission of taxes from all the villages belonging to Kōlāla-sīme, which belongs to the māḍa-gauḍike of the donors Kempaṇṇa-nāyaka and Nandyoppa-nāyaka, agents of Bayirappa-nāyaka. Also records the grant of a village Vommachihalli. belonging to Kōlāla-nāḍa-sīme, as daṇḍige-umbaḥi to Situkal Gaṅgappa-nāyaka, for the nāḍa-gauḍike , by the same donors.
